hotels.scores:
THE NIGHT LOG (auteur): 52/70
- Originality 8. A 3D section of the visitor's own property, rebuilt live by the agent's client tools and lit by the agent's body, is new. The night-of-hours frame (Clos des Sens, Primland, the old site's own story), the lift doors and the circular progress dial are known devices.
- Premium feel 8. A monograph drawing in champagne light on forest with one warm light source is quiet luxury. Hatching, leader lines and sliding lift doors together risk a busy, technical-blueprint look.
- Clarity/usability 7. Normal vertical scroll and a DOM log column keep reading easy. A talk target that travels, leader lines and lift-door jumps add load. The global J/K shortcuts breach WCAG 2.1.4.
- Conversion 9. Price, ledger and guarantee are above the fold. House, then handover, then a prefilled registration card is a real funnel, with the decision made at dawn.
- Feasibility 6. A five-archetype building generator, MeshPhysical transmission refracting the whole building, lift doors and stills captured at build time are a lot to build for one niche.
- Performance 6. A full-viewport canvas plus a transmission pass of the building every frame is the most expensive path of the three.
- Accessibility 8. DOM reading order, an hour list that works without JS, text measured on a scrim, and real transcripts.

THE NIGHT GLASS (inventor): 53/70
- Originality 9. The agent's body as the page's crown and slider, a clock shared with her second hand, and refraction used as translation: I know of no precedent for any of them.
- Premium feel 9. One rendered jewel over a gilt hairline elevation. The most restrained of the three.
- Clarity/usability 6. Turning a glass to scroll is a new mental model: a horizontal drag drives vertical travel, and one object carries ringing, turning and time. It needs hints and analytics.
- Conversion 8. The offer plaque is above the fold. The registration card comes at 3 am, before the price, which is the wrong order.
- Feasibility 6. The analytic glass shader (3–4 days), aligning the translation plate and coupling to Lenis are hard but bounded. The elevation needs a hand-drawn SVG.
- Performance 8. One quad sampling a half-resolution backdrop costs less than a transmission pass.
- Accessibility 7. role=slider is elegant, but a slider that scrolls the whole document is unusual for assistive tech.

THE NIGHT EDITION (editor): 45/70
- Originality 8. A live concertina of real, selectable type lit by a voice lamp is new. Horizontal scroll and the book metaphor are award-site staples.
- Premium feel 9. Leather, foil, letterpress and lamplight are the most tactile of the three. The leather desk edges toward skeuomorphic kitsch.
- Clarity/usability 5. Vertical input drives horizontal hinged pages, the reading windows are 487 px wide, forms sit on transformed planes, and find-in-page breaks.
- Conversion 7. The belly band and its persistent tab are excellent. Horizontal reading loses skimmers.
- Feasibility 4. A DOM page chain kept aligned to GL planes, soft text in Safari, focus-driven page turns and three rendering tiers make this the riskiest build.
- Performance 6. Up to seven promoted 3D layers, plus desk shading and transmission.
- Accessibility 6. Lay flat helps, but the default view is a transformed horizontal book.

VERDICT
The Night Log is the spine, even though The Night Glass scores one point higher. The Night Glass's best parts (the glass, the hour ring, refraction as translation, the cheaper renderer) can be grafted. The Night Log's strengths (funnel, reading model, accessibility, and the proof of the visitor's own house answered all night) cannot.

Grafts from The Night Glass:
- The glass whose champagne stays level, now explained by a gimbal.
- The hour ring as the page's crown and its Night Dial.
- Amariya's second hand as the follow prompt.
- Translation through the glass.
- Scenario chips.
- 'Welcome back, The Harbour House'.
- The analytic glass renderer. It is cheaper than transmission and fixes the 'crystal ball' look of today's preview.

Grafts from The Night Edition:
- The telephone-message slip as the dock, with printed state ticks.
- A 'Do Not Disturb' hanger as the Pause motion control.
- 'Send this handover to your GM'.
- Honest minutes for both cases (missed calls only, and every call).
- OTA commission shown only from the visitor's own rate.
- Room light that swells with her syllables.
- An etched monogram, so you can see the glass rotate.
- Running heads that carry the house name.

Cut:
- The concertina book and the pendant lamp.
- Lift doors.
- Global single-key shortcuts.
- Blurred headline reveals.
- Carrying the light by drag distance, replaced by a bail handle.
- Five archetype meshes, replaced by one parametric kit.
hotels.novelty_check:
All three concepts arrived at the same frame (a night of hours, a champagne orb with liquid, a key board), which is a warning sign. Each derivative element is checked below and pushed further or cut.

1. A night told in hours. Derivative of Clos des Sens (episodes), Explore Primland ('3 a.m.') and the old site's own story.
PUSHED: the hour is the data model, not a skin. It is the URL (#h-2348), the slider's value, the camera rail, the light, window occupancy, and the target of the agent's navigation. The prologue opens at the visitor's real hour, and the house is theirs.

2. A liquid-in-a-sphere shader with a tilting meniscus. A Codrops/Shadertoy staple ('potion bottle').
PUSHED: the gimbal turns the level surface from a shader trick into the physical reason to handle the object. The liquid is the voice-state display and reads without colour: a pour for connecting, a mirror-still surface for listening, a vortex for thinking, effervescence for speaking. It is the scene's only light source, and it refracts and translates the world behind it.
CUT: the cloudy nebula core that made today's preview read as a crystal ball.

3. The cursor stirring the orb (BlueYard's GPU fluid). Cut as a simulation. The visitor's circling becomes liquid spin through ordinary physics, so the 'sommelier's swirl' emerges without a detector or a fluid solver.

4. Glass bending text behind it (Noomo Labs, GetLayers 'Frozen Globe').
PUSHED to a change of meaning: the guest's sentence changes language as it passes behind the glass. The sentence is routed through the empty upper half of the globe so it stays legible. Where it dips into the champagne, the liquid inverts and magnifies it like a real glass, on purpose.

5. Line-drawn buildings: architecture-studio blueprint reveals and isometric hotel cutaways.
PUSHED: a true section with poché, never blueprint blue and never isometric. It is rebuilt from the visitor's own answers through the agent's tools, and the agent's light falls on it physically.
CUT: hatch geometry (it becomes a shader), five archetype meshes (one parametric kit), and furniture geometry (sprites).

6. Callout leader lines (Apple-style product tours). Restrained to architectural annotations on desktop only, never crossing text. Phones get room tags inside the band.

7. A circular scroll-progress dial. A common progress widget.
PUSHED: the dial is a physical part of the lantern. You can turn it, it docks in the cornice, and it carries the agent's second hand.
CUT: the separate needle dial.

8. Lift-door transitions.
CUT: they are theatrical, full-screen, add vestibular load, and serve a rare action. Replaced by 'lights down': the porter dims the house and the lantern relights the target room, in 240 + 420 ms, and instantly under reduced motion.

9. A brass key board. A hotel cliché, present in all three concepts.
KEPT only because it encodes real data: issued, held and open counts from HubSpot, plus the agent's recommendation lifting a key toward the visitor. No names appear without consent. The DOM list is the real control. Phones use a cheaper matcap version.

10. Per-letter or per-word blur reveals (SplitText). The stock award reveal, and an AA risk.
CUT: text is present from the first paint. One gilt light-sweep crosses the H1.

11. A skippable cinematic intro (KHUFU'S).
KEPT at 1.6 s: the porter's light plus the pour. It never blocks, has no percentage preloader, and is skipped on return visits.

12. The Night Edition's concertina book, belly band and pendant lamp.
CUT as structure. The band survives as the persistent key-fob tag 'Take a key · 30 open'. The editorial craft survives as running heads and the printable handover.

13. A giant outlined footer wordmark. An award trope, flagged in the old-site critique.
REPLACED by a small engraved brass plate beside the door, read by a raking light.

14. Banned clichés: glass pills, gradient blobs, aurora on black, centred SaaS sections, three-tier cards. None remain. Features are rooms, pricing is a key rack, the form is a registration card, and the dock is a telephone message slip.

15. Film grain. Common.
KEPT at the existing 6% on the page only, never over log text, and removed under prefers-contrast: more.

16. Too many gestures (turn, shake, swirl, carry, tap, pendulum swing). A novelty-of-interaction trap.
REDUCED to three verbs on three physical parts: turn the glass, turn the ring, lift the bail. Tap rings her. Shake-to-fizz and swirl fall out of the physics rather than being separate gestures.

17. 'Turn the glass to scroll'. It risked a gimmick that fights rotation.
MOVED from the glass to the ring. Turning the glass is always just play. The ring is optional and fully mirrored by scroll, the slider keys and the Night index, and a config flag can make it decorative if analytics show confusion.

18. Personalised 'your name here' pages. Common in SaaS email.
PUSHED: the personalisation is structural and spatial (floors, bays, restaurant, roof, canopy), it is spoken back by the scripted calls, and it is printed on the handover.

final.angle: The auteur concept (The Night Log) is the spine. From the inventor it takes the gimballed glass, the hour ring as the page's crown, the agent's second hand and translation by refraction. From the editor it takes the telephone-message slip, the GM handover, the Do Not Disturb pause and the running heads.
final.one_line: One night at the visitor's own hotel or restaurant, drawn as a lit architectural section. You scroll, or turn the lantern's hour ring, from 18:00 to 07:45. Amariya is a gimballed champagne lantern you can turn, tap and carry. She answers each call room by room, rebuilds the house as you describe it, leaves the morning numbers on your desk and hangs thirty founding keys behind the desk at dawn.
final.big_idea:
THE DEVICE: TIME RUNS THE PAGE
Scroll is the clock of one night at the visitor's own house, 18:00 to 07:45. Each chapter is an entry in the night log: an hour, a room and a call. The hour is the data model, not decoration. It sets:
- the URL (#h-2348);
- the value of the navigation slider;
- the camera's place on its rail;
- the colour of the sky;
- which windows are lit;
- what the agent's section names point to.

THE STAGE
One continuous WebGL world, never a stack of sections: an architect's section cut through the visitor's own hotel or restaurant, drawn in champagne ink on forest. Cut walls carry hatched poché and rooms sit behind each cut. A lift shaft runs up the middle, the restaurant is on the ground floor, the night desk is in the lobby and a terrace is on the roof.

Copy lives in the DOM, in a log column, and a hairline annotation ties each entry to its room, as on a monograph drawing. Features are not pills or cards; each feature is a room where a call happens.

THE CHARACTER
Amariya is a gimballed champagne lantern. A blown-glass globe, half full of luminous champagne, hangs on two pins inside a brass gimbal. The gimbal's outer ring is engraved with the hours of the night, and a bail (carry handle) sits on top.

Gimballed ship's lamps keep their oil level whatever the sea does. Here the champagne's surface stays level however the globe is turned, and that is exactly what makes people want to handle it.

Three parts, three verbs:
- Turn the glass. It rotates with weight and inertia and rights itself. The champagne sloshes, fizzes when shaken and swirls when you circle it.
- Turn the ring. The ring is the page's clock: turning it walks the night, and the page scrolls with it, with watch-crown detents at every hour. When the lantern leaves the hero, the ring lifts off and docks in the cornice as the Night Dial, so the same object is the navigation all the way down.
- Lift the bail (desktop). Carry the light to any lit room and the night jumps to that hour.

Tap the glass, as a host taps a flute before a toast, and she answers.

She is also the scene's only warm light. The rooms she visits are lit by her, and the light swells with her syllables.

THE PAYOFF: THE HOUSE IS THEIRS
Say or type 'The Harbour House, 80 rooms, a restaurant', or tap one scenario chip, and the section rebuilds:
- floors rise and bays multiply;
- the restaurant floor appears;
- the name is gilded on the canopy and in the running head;
- every scripted call greets guests in that name.

In the lobby hour, the guest's sentence slides behind her glass and reads in Spanish through it: translation by refraction.

Agent and visitor share one clock. If she wants to show something while you are reading, a second hand appears on the ring, pointing at her hour, and you choose whether to follow.

The ROI is the morning handover note on the owner's desk. The founders' offer is thirty brass keys on the rack behind the desk. The application is a registration card.

WHY IT HAS NEVER BEEN DONE
- Hotel sites show rooms to guests, and AI-receptionist sites show a blob and three pricing cards. None renders the visitor's own property as a live section that the voice agent rebuilds and moves through, using its client tools during the conversation.
- No voice agent's body has ever been, at once, the page's light source, its navigation crown and its talk button.
- Glass that bends text exists (Noomo Labs; GetLayers' Frozen Globe). Glass that changes the language of what passes behind it does not.
- An honest scarcity ledger has never been a physical object driven by CRM counts.

REFERENCES, AND HOW IT GOES BEYOND THEM
- Explore Primland (a real-time place, day/night, '3 a.m.'): here the place is the visitor's own property, and the night opens at their real hour.
- Clos des Sens (one night told in episodes): here the episodes are calls, mapped one to one to the agent's feature keys.
- Son Daven (two-colour discipline, one scroll scene per section, financial indicators): here forest and champagne only, the lantern as the one warm light, and the morning handover as the indicators.
- BlueYard, Cartesia, GetLayers (the cursor stirs, listening draws inward, product states): here a real liquid in a gimballed glass, whose surface, bubbles and spin show every voice state without relying on colour.
- Noomo Labs and Frozen Globe (text bent behind glass): here text translated behind glass.
- KHUFU'S (a skippable cinematic intro): here a 1.6 s porter's light and a pour that never block content.
- Neko and Biograph (status per market; price and what holds your place on one card): here the key rack, with price, guarantee and an honest count on one object.
- The Bend Club, Designjoy and Default (a small list, a guarantee under the price, silent qualification, a calendar on the page): here the registration card, then qualification, then a 20-minute call reserved on the page.
final.structure:
FIXED LAYERS
(a) The cornice: 72px tall on desktop, 56px on phones, with a 1px brass rule.
- Left: 'Amariya' in Ranade 500.
- Centre: the Night Dial. It is the top arc of the lantern's hour ring, seen through a 240×64 brass window. The hours roll under a fixed index, with a caption below such as '23:48 · Room 214'. It appears once the ring has docked.
- Right: the switcher 'For hotels & restaurants ▾', the Sound toggle, Pause motion (a Do Not Disturb door hanger), and the key-fob tag 'Take a key · 30 open', which retires once the key rack is on screen.

(b) The house: a full-bleed, fixed WebGL2 canvas behind everything, aria-hidden.

(c) The desk slip: a 72px full-width bar at the bottom, styled as a telephone message pad. Body padding-bottom and scroll-padding-bottom reserve its height, so it never covers content or focus.

(d) The annotation layer: a fixed SVG overlay, decorative, desktop only.

Content is ordinary DOM in reading order. On desktop it sits in the log column (grid columns 9–12, max 440px) over a forest-950 scrim at 88%. A running head sits above it: 'Your house · tonight', which becomes 'The Harbour House · the night of Friday 16 October' once the house is named. Scrolling is native, with Lenis on fine pointers only.

SCROLL MODEL
The NightClock maps scrollY to minutes since 18:00 (0 to 825) through an offset table. The table is cached and rebuilt only on ResizeObserver and fonts.ready.

Every night chapter has the same ten beats, so something changes every 10%:
- 0–10%: the lantern arrives and the ring's index settles.
- 10–20%: the room phone rings (a UK double-ring LED) and its annotation draws.
- 20–30%: the lantern docks and the window lights with a filament flicker.
- 30–70%: the call lines appear, revealed at scroll thresholds and completed in real time.
- 70–80%: the outcome stamp presses in, and a line lights in the back-office ledger.
- 80–90%: the room settles to a glow.
- 90–100%: the camera rides the shaft and the ring rolls to the next hour.

CHAPTERS (time · title · id · agent section · scroll length)

0. NOW · PROLOGUE · #welcome · welcome · 100svh
The house as it is right now where the visitor is. About 40% of windows are lit in the evening and 12% between 2 and 5 am; daytime visitors see it at dusk.
- Eyebrow, a live sentence: 'It's 1:04 am where you are, at your [boutique hotel ▾].' The bracketed part is a button. It opens four scenario chips (Boutique hotel · Resort · Restaurant · Hotel with a restaurant). A chip sets hotel_type and rebuilds the house at once, with no form. Static HTML reads 'It's 2:14 am…'.
- H1: 'Every call tonight, answered.' It sits on the drawing's ground line, a full-width hairline at 64% of the viewport height that serves as its typographic baseline.
- The basement band below the ground line, left: the lede; the fob-shaped primary 'Take a founding key'; 'Ring for Amariya'; and the text links 'or write to her' and 'or just look around'.
- The basement band, right: '$2,500 once · first 30 hotels & restaurants · 30 of 30 keys on the rack · Live in 7 days or your money back.'
- The lantern sits at the lobby desk, right of centre, inside its ring. A coaster caption 'Tap the glass · turn the ring' shows until first use.
- Everything above fits above the fold at 1440×900. At 390×844, price, ledger and guarantee are visible within 1.5 screens.

I. 18:00 · YOUR HOUSE · #house (alias #profile) · profile · 120svh
'Which house are we keeping tonight?' The Property Card holds six fields. As they change, the house rebuilds: floors rise, bays multiply, the restaurant floor appears or goes, and the name is gilded on the canopy and in the running head.
A live teaser under the card reads 'On a night like this, about 8 calls your desk would miss', with a link: 'See the morning handover'.

II. 19:52 · THE RESTAURANT, SECOND SEATING · feature 'bookings' · 100svh
'The maître d' has both hands full.'
- A caller asks for a table for four at 20:30.
- A nut allergy is handed to the kitchen: 'the team will confirm what they can prepare'.
- The stamp reads 'Booked · Table 12 · 20:30'.
- Hotel houses add a log line: '19:58 · A room for Friday, booked direct.'

III. 21:15 · THE LOBBY · feature 'multilingual' · 140svh
A close-up on the desk, with the lantern large.
- Nine gold phone lines run in from the city lights. Greetings rise where they touch the desk, the visitor's own browser language first.
- The guest's sentences pass behind the glass and read in Spanish through it.
- The stamp reads 'Reserva confirmada · 1 noche'.

IV. 23:48 · ROOM 214, THE ROOF TERRACE · feature 'upsells' · 100svh
'Is the pool open late?' It ends with a cabana booked for 21:00 tomorrow.
A restaurant-only house sees '23:10 · A private dining enquiry for 14' instead.

V. 01:04 · THE NIGHT DESK · feature 'answering' · 120svh
'A late check-in, answered on the first ring.'
- If the visitor is up between midnight and 5 am, their own time stands in, and the ring's 'now' pin glows.
- A second entry, '03:10 · A delicate one', shows a warm transfer to the night manager with a one-line summary.
- The closing line follows the time of day: 'Your night team sleeps.' at night, 'Your team stays with the guest in front of them.' by day.

VI. 02:30 · THE BACK OFFICE, THE NIGHT AUDIT · feature 'integrations' · 100svh
'The audit finds nothing to fix.' Tonight's bookings light one by one as ledger lines that are already in the PMS or reservation book. System names are shown only once the owner confirms them.

VII. 05:40 · ROOM 507 · feature 'guest_requests' · 100svh
A taxi to the airport at 06:15 and a 14:00 late checkout. The routed requests drop as slips stamped Concierge and Front office.
A restaurant-only house sees '06:40 · A scarf left at table 9' instead.

VIII. 07:00 · THE MORNING HANDOVER · #handover · 120svh
Dawn. The windows go out one by one, and the ROI note lies on the owner's desk with the pale lantern beside it.

IX. 07:30 · THE KEY RACK · #keys (alias #pricing) · pricing · 140svh
The camera pushes into the rack behind the desk: thirty brass keys, the price, the honest ledger, the guarantee plate, and 'after the thirtieth key, plans from $299 a month'.

X. 07:45 · REGISTRATION · #register (aliases #apply and #demo) · demo · natural height
The canvas holds a dawn still.

XI. QUESTIONS AT THE DESK · #faq · natural height
The canvas holds a still at 15%.

XII. CHECKOUT · footer · 90svh
The camera descends to the street at sunrise and stops at the brass plate beside the door.

The page is about 13 screens on desktop. The six room chapters replace the old story, features stage and live-call card in about 6.6 screens, against 8 on the old site.

NAVIGATION
The Night Dial is nav[aria-label='The night']. It holds:
- the ring as a role=slider (with JS);
- an ordered list of hour links that always exists and works without JS. The links show in the Night index.

The Night index is a native <dialog> styled as an in-room directory card. It lists every hour row with its room and a one-line summary (aria-current on the current hour), the switcher, Sound, Pause, Ring and Write.

How jumps move:
- To the next or previous hour: a Lenis scroll of 900–1400 ms.
- More than one chapter away (dial, index, agent, follow, carry): 'lights down'. The house dims, the jump happens, and the lantern relights the target room.
- Under reduced motion or Pause: an instant cut.
- Every jump updates the hash with history.replaceState.

Phones: a time chip '23:48 ▾' in the cornice opens the index.

Polite agent navigation: if Amariya wants to move within 2.5 s of the visitor's own input, she does not scroll. Her second hand appears on the ring, pointing at her hour, and a slip note appears above the desk: 'Amariya would like to show you 23:48 · Room 214 — Follow'.
final.orb:
ROLE
Amariya's body, the talk button, the scene's only warm light, and, through its ring, the page's clock and navigation.

THE OBJECT
- A blown-glass globe of radius R, half full of luminous champagne.
- The globe hangs on two brass pins (at 3 and 9 o'clock) inside a thin brass gimbal, with a bail on top.
- An etched frosted band and an 'A' monogram are cut into the glass (a roughness mask), so its rotation is always visible.
- The engraved outer hour ring is a DOM SVG bezel aligned to the projected circle. It stays crisp and accessible, and it can fly to the cornice.

A transparent circular <button> follows the globe's projected centre and radius. It writes one transform per frame and reads no layout.
- Its visible label equals its accessible name: 'Ring for Amariya', then 'Connecting…', then 'End the call'.
- aria-describedby: 'Tap the glass or press Enter to talk. Drag or use the arrow keys to turn the glass. The hour ring is in the Night Dial.'
- Focus ring: 2px champagne-300 at R + 6px, plus a 1px forest-950 outer ring, measured at 3:1 or better over lit areas.

SIZES
- Prologue: R = min(19svh, 38vw), with the ring out to 1.30R.
- Travelling between rooms: R = 36–48px. Below a projected radius of 22px (a target under 44px), the button becomes tabindex −1 and pointer-events: none, and the desk slip carries Ring.
- Lobby close-up (21:15): R = min(30svh, 34vw).
- Handover: 80px, resting on the note.
- Footer: 64px, in a bracket by the door.

ZONE 1: THE GLASS (r ≤ 1.0R). TURN IT.
Rotation:
- Drag rotates the globe: gain 0.0085 rad/px on both axes.
- Yaw is unlimited. Pitch is clamped to ±0.9 rad, with a tanh rubber band beyond.
- ω is capped at 9 rad/s. Release velocity comes from the last 80 ms of samples.
- After release it decays freely as ω·e^(−2.2·dt), resting in about 1.5 s.

Self-righting:
- 400 ms after release, pitch and roll return to the rest pose (pitch 0, tilt 0.06 rad) on a spring with k 14 s⁻² and c 5.2 s⁻¹ (ζ ≈ 0.69, one soft overshoot).
- After 3 s idle, a yaw 'untwist' spring (k 2.2 s⁻², ζ 0.4) turns the monogram back to face the visitor.

The liquid stays level (the gimbal):
- Surface tilt α is a damped oscillator: ωn 6.9 rad/s (about 1.1 Hz), ζ 0.14.
- It is forced by the globe's lateral acceleration (0.0016 rad per px/s²) and its angular acceleration (−0.02·dω/dt). It is capped at ±0.42 rad.
- A hard throw sloshes 4–5 times and settles in about 3 s.

Spin and vortex:
- Liquid spin follows the glass's yaw rate with τ 0.42 s and decays with τ 1.8 s.
- Spin dips the centre into a vortex of depth 0.022·ω²·R, at most 0.16R.

Perlage (the bubbles):
- Bubbles rise from three nucleation points fixed to the glass, so they turn with it and show the rotation.
- Base rate 24 beads/s, plus 200/s × |ω| when shaken (shake-to-fizz falls out of the physics).
- Ring buffer: 600 on desktop, 220 on phones.
- Beads always rise toward world-up at 0.18–0.32 R/s and grow 1.0→1.7× as they rise. Each pop leaves a tiny ring on the surface.
- Gold flecks drift with Brownian motion below the surface.

Hover (within 1.6R, no button pressed):
- The globe leans up to 0.12 rad toward the cursor (τ 250 ms).
- The core warms by up to +12%, like a glass cupped in the hand.
- The flecks curl around the cursor's velocity (amplitude 0.04).
- The cursor's circulation around the glass adds to the liquid's spin: spin += 0.15·Γ, capped at 1.6 rad/s. Circling the glass like a sommelier makes the swirl with no special detector.

Tap:
- A press shorter than 250 ms that moves under 8px rings her: requestStart('voice') when idle, end when live.
- With Sound on: a crystal 'ting' with partials at 1, 2.76, 5.40 and 8.93 × 1,568 Hz, a 1.2 s exponential decay and gain 0.05. The AudioContext is created inside the gesture, which fixes the old iOS chime bug.
- With Sound off: a silent ripple on the meniscus.

ZONE 2: THE RING (1.08R to 1.30R; the DOM bezel). TURN THE NIGHT.
Scale: 18:00 to 07:45 is 825 minutes over 330° (0.4° per minute), with a 30° clasp at the top under the bail.

Drag:
- Drag tangentially at 0.45°/px on desktop, about 730px for the whole night.
- Release velocity comes from the last 80 ms, clamped to ±720°/s, and decays with τ 0.42 s.

Detents:
- Below 30°/s a detent spring takes over (k 90 s⁻², c 14 s⁻¹, ζ ≈ 0.74; about 3% overshoot; settles in under 450 ms).
- It snaps to the nearest chapter if one is within 18° (45 minutes), otherwise to the nearest quarter hour (6°).
- Ticks flash as they pass. With Sound on, each detent clicks, with a 4 ms vibration where supported.

While the ring is dragged or coasting, it drives the page: angle → minutes → scrollY through the NightClock map → lenis.scrollTo(y, {immediate: true}). Any wheel, key or touch scroll cancels the coast.

Marks on the ring:
- An ivory 'now' pin at the visitor's real hour, when that hour falls inside the night.
- Amariya's second hand, a hairline with a diamond tip, for the follow prompt.

Docking: when the lantern leaves the prologue (60% of its span), the ring does a 900 ms FLIP into the cornice window and becomes the Night Dial. It returns around the glass in the lobby close-up.

ZONE 3: THE BAIL (desktop, fine pointer only). CARRY THE LIGHT.
- Dragging the bail lifts the lantern into carry. It follows the pointer on a critically damped spring (k 120, c 22, ζ = 1.0), banks into its direction of travel by up to 0.12 rad, and the champagne sloshes from the acceleration.
- Rooms you can drop it in show dotted outlines. A room within 70px warms up (warmth 0→0.4 in 200 ms).
- Drop on a room: the night travels to that hour, with lights down if it is far.
- Drop elsewhere: it springs home (k 60, c 11, ζ ≈ 0.71).
- Esc cancels.
- The cursor shows 'grab' on the glass, 'ew-resize' along the ring and 'move' on the bail.
- Carry is an extra, never the only route: the dial, the index and the links reach every room.

TOUCH
- The host has touch-action: pan-y, so vertical swipes always scroll the page.
- A horizontal swipe (|dx| > 1.2|dy| after 8px of slop) turns the glass in yaw at once, with the same inertia.
- A 300 ms long-press grabs it fully (pitch and yaw). This uses pointer capture, a non-passive touchmove that calls preventDefault, and navigator.vibrate(8) where supported. The first time, a hint reads 'Hold to tilt the glass'.
- A tap rings her.
- A two-finger twist swirls the liquid at the twist rate.
- On phones the ring is decorative: tapping it opens the Night index. Carry is off.

KEYBOARD
The glass button:
- Enter or Space: ring when idle, end when live.
- ←/→: yaw impulse of ±1.6 rad/s. ↑/↓: pitch steps of 0.21 rad on the spring. Shift doubles both.
- Home: upright. Esc: release.
The ring is the slider in the cornice nav: ←/↓ go back 15 minutes, →/↑ go forward 15 minutes, PageUp/PageDown move a chapter, Home/End go to 18:00 and 07:45.
There are no global single-character shortcuts. Rotation is decorative and is never announced.

VOICE STATES
State is shown by shape and motion first and colour second, so it reads in still frames and for colour-blind visitors. OrbState is extended to idle | connecting | listening | thinking | speaking, plus muted, tone and a level from two sources. The level envelope keeps stage.ts's 40 ms attack and 200 ms release; states blend over 250 ms.
- Idle: fill 56%, breathing ±1.2% at 0.15 Hz, perlage 24/s, flecks drifting, core 1.0, room light 1.0.
- Connecting (the pour): the fill rises 40%→58% over 1.2 s (easeOutCubic). The bubbles gather into one central bead chain at 30/s. The ring's index pulses at 1 Hz, and the globe dips 18px, leaning in.
- Listening (she holds her breath): the surface goes mirror-still. The visitor's mic level (getInputVolume) sends inward rings across it (amplitude 0.012R × level). Bubbles slow to 3/s. The core dims 25% and cools toward ivory, and the flecks gather to the centre.
- Thinking: a slow vortex (liquid spin 1.4 rad/s) that dips the centre by 3%. The flecks spiral and the bead strings helix. The core flickers like a candle within ±4%, below any flash threshold.
- Speaking (her voice is effervescence): bubbles at 24 + 300·amp per second; outward surface rings at syllable peaks, at most 6/s; core 0.7 + 1.0·amp; flecks lift 8%. The light in the room she occupies is multiplied by (1 + 0.35·amp): the lit room breathes with her words, never changing by more than 45% and never faster than syllables. When getOutputByteFrequencyData is available, low frequencies drive the surface waves, mids the bubble rate and highs glints on the flecks.
- Muted: a fine frost ring forms on the glass at the meniscus, a shape cue alongside the slip's tick.
- Tone, from the ElevenLabs v3 tags (TONES map unchanged, τ 250 ms):
  - bright: bubbles ×1.4, core +15%, hue toward champagne-100;
  - soft: ×0.85, core −15%;
  - calm: cooler and paler toward ivory, ×0.95;
  - warm: the default.

SCROLL AND TRAVEL
- Lenis velocity sloshes the liquid like a glass carried upstairs: the pitch rate gains −v·0.0006, clamped to ±0.6 rad/s. Bubbles rise 10% faster above 1,200 px/s.
- Between rooms the lantern follows a critically damped spring (ω 5 rad/s, settling in about 0.9 s). It banks up to 0.12 rad into its travel and leaves 100 additive gold motes in its light cone.

UNDER REDUCED MOTION OR PAUSE
No inertia, slosh, bubbles or lean. The arrow keys and drag still turn the glass in 15° steps, and the ring still turns the night. A still frame is redrawn on every state change and shows the state through fill, surface and light.
final.three_d:
ONE CONTEXT, ONE RENDERER
HouseStage generalises today's OrbStage: the renderer loop, DPR cap, hidden-tab pause, one-time degrade with no shader recompiles, and context-loss handling. It owns a single WebGL2 canvas for the whole page. All three.js parts share one scheduler, and per-chapter culling draws only what the current hour needs.

1. THE HOUSE: A PARAMETRIC SECTION KIT, NOT ARCHETYPE MESHES
Parameters:
- floors = clamp(ceil(rooms/14), 2, 9) for hotels;
- bays: 3–12;
- ground floor: lobby + restaurant | restaurant only | lobby only;
- roof: terrace + pool | garden | plain | pitched;
- width class.
The four scenario chips are presets:
- Boutique: 5 floors × 6 bays.
- Resort: 3 floors × 12 bays, with a pool deck.
- Restaurant: one storey with a private dining room above.
- Hotel with a restaurant: 7 floors × 5 bays.

Geometry and shading:
- Slabs and walls are merged boxes.
- Cut faces use a poché shader: forest-900 fill with a 45° champagne hatch from step(fract((x+y)·density)). There is no hatch geometry.
- Rooms are depth planes holding silhouette sprites from one 1024² atlas: bed, dining table, chairs, lamp, cloche, wine glass, and a phone with an emissive LED.
- Windows are one InstancedMesh with at most 220 instances. Per-instance lit, occupancy and seed values drive a filament flicker: 0→0.6 in 80 ms, →0.4 in 60 ms, →1 in 500 ms.
- Every edge is merged into one LineSegments of about 2–3k segments. Its shader fades lines with depth and brightens them near the lantern: ink drawn in light.
- The canopy name is a CanvasTexture in Cormorant Garamond 600, redrawn only when hotel_name changes.

Rebuilds take under 8 ms and are debounced by 150 ms. The new house rises through a uRise clip plane with a 1px gold seam over 900 ms.

Lighting: no three.js lights. The shader computes:
- the lantern term: warmth·(n·l)/(1 + d²·6)·(1 + 0.35·amp);
- window glow;
- a dawn directional light driven by the NightClock;
- 3% blue-noise grain.
Output luminance behind the log column is clamped to a generator-measured envelope, so text contrast can never fail.

2. SKY AND CITY
- A backdrop plane graded by the clock: dusk forest-teal → deep night → dawn apricot. The apricot comes from a new decorative 'dawn' ramp in the generator.
- About 300 star points, shown only between 23:00 and 04:30.
- A distant city line of instanced windows (at most 400), where calls come from.
- Headlight sweeps cross the street plane every 18–30 s as idle life.

3. PHONE LINES (21:15)
Nine gold line strips run from city points to the desk phone, with a pulse travelling along each line's UV at 1.4 units/s. DOM greeting labels, each with a lang attribute, are projected to the ends of the lines. They keep the old cadence: one every 1.05 s, a 2.1 s life, alternating sides.

4. THE LANTERN: AN ANALYTIC GLASS ON ONE CAMERA-FACING QUAD
This replaces the MeshPhysical transmission in champagne.ts, which stays only as a fallback. Per pixel:
- a ray–sphere hit;
- a thin glass shell: IOR 1.5, Schlick Fresnel with F0 0.04;
- a world-level liquid plane, intersected analytically, carrying a ripple height field (the sum of up to 6 analytic rings);
- the liquid: IOR 1.34 with Beer–Lambert absorption σ = (0.9, 1.3, 3.2)/R, because champagne absorbs blue most;
- a bright meniscus line where the surface meets the glass;
- two analytic softboxes and a rim light;
- an inner emissive core;
- anti-aliased edges using fwidth;
- dispersion as three samples of the backdrop texture, on desktop only.

The backdrop is a texture the refracted rays read. It is rendered with camera.setViewOffset over the lantern's screen rectangle only, at 0.5 scale (0.35 on coarse pointers), so its cost scales with the lantern's size.

Other parts:
- The etched band and monogram come from a roughness mask.
- Bubbles and flecks are two Points buffers clipped by the surface height.
- The gimbal arc, pins and bail are low-poly brass: MeshStandardMaterial, metalness 1, roughness 0.3, lit by the RoomEnvironment PMREM already built in champagne.ts.
- Glow is one additive halo sprite; there is no bloom.
- Both quality tiers are precompiled with renderer.compile at boot.

THE TRANSLATION PLATE (21:15)
- A text plane drawn on a 2D canvas, so the browser shapes the text (Arabic and Japanese use system fonts).
- It is on layer 2, which is rendered only into the lantern's backdrop pass, never to the screen.
- The DOM sentence is masked out inside the glass circle with a CSS radial-gradient mask driven by --ox, --oy and --or.
- The sentence is routed through the empty upper 44% of the globe, where the shell's mild barrel distortion keeps it legible. Where it dips into the champagne, it inverts and magnifies as a real glass would.
- An sr-only list carries every translation.

5. THE KEY RACK (07:30)
- A wooden board plane with 30 brass hooks.
- The keys (bow, blade and fob, about 400 triangles each) are one InstancedMesh: metalness 1, roughness 0.32, lit by the PMREM. Fob numbers 01–30 come from a 512² atlas.
- Each key is a damped pendulum: θ'' = −(g/L)·sinθ − 1.6·θ', with g/L 81.7 (about 1.44 Hz).
- Cursor velocity within 120px pushes nearby keys (impulse v × 0.002 rad/s per px/s, clamped to ±3 rad/s).
- Hover, or focus on the matching item in the DOM ledger list, swings a key and turns its fob to face the visitor.

Ledger states:
- Issued: the key is removed and replaced by an engraved plate reading 'Issued' (the house name only with that house's consent).
- Held: the fob is turned and tinted champagne-700, with a 'Held' tag.
- Open: the key hangs.

When Amariya recommends the licence, the next open key lifts off its hook and turns toward the visitor. Phones use a matcap material and skip the PMREM.

6. DAWN
At 07:00 the windows go out in a seeded order over 4 s, the lantern pales to ivory, and a raking sunrise crosses the facade.

7. THE BRASS PLATE (footer)
A plane carrying a normal map baked at build time: 'Amariya' set in Ranade, turned into a height map, then a Sobel pass, stored as a 1024×256 PNG. It is lit by the sunrise and by a raking light that follows the cursor, or the focused control for keyboard users. On touch, the light sweeps slowly by itself, and Pause stops it. The wordmark is engraved, not outlined.

8. LIGHTS DOWN (DOM, not WebGL)
The scrim rises to 100% forest-950 in 240 ms, holds 120 ms while the jump happens, then falls in 420 ms while the lantern relights the target room.

BUDGET
- At most 30 draw calls, 80k triangles and 20 MB of textures.
- No post-processing composer.
- Per-chapter culling: the rack draws only in chapter IX, the plate only in XII, the threads only in III.
- After 20 s with no input, scroll or voice, the loop drops to 30 fps, and to 15 fps after 60 s. Any input restores the full rate.

FALLBACKS
- Without WebGL2, or after a second slow-device trigger: a pre-rendered AVIF still of the default house for each chapter (about 60 KB each, captured at build time with Playwright), with the canopy name overlaid in the DOM.
- The lantern becomes a CSS still: a clear upper half, a champagne lower half with a bright meniscus line, the pins and the bail, scaled by --level.
- The ring stays an SVG slider and still turns the night.

final.motion_language:
PARADIGM: TIME-SCRUB
Scroll is the clock of the night. The camera never cuts inside the house; it rides one rail through the section. Within a chapter it moves sideways. Between chapters it climbs the lift shaft on an S-curve, smoothstepped over the last 30% of each span. Scroll-to-camera smoothing has τ 120 ms.

One Director module owns time. Each frame it reads the Lenis scroll value once, sets the NightClock, and writes the camera, the light and the CSS variables (--t, --gx/--gy, --ox/--oy/--or). DOM beats are GSAP 3.13 core timelines whose progress the Director sets. There is no ScrollTrigger, no second scroll owner, and no layout read in the frame loop.

THREE MOTION FAMILIES
- Light and liquid (camera, lantern travel, sky, room light): cubic-bezier(.45,0,.2,1), 900–1600 ms, plus physical springs for the glass (constants in the orb section).
- Mechanical (ring detents, keys, stamps, slip ticks, fob, hanger): cubic-bezier(.34,1.32,.64,1), 180–320 ms, about 3–4% overshoot. The keys are pendulums at 1.44 Hz with damping 1.6/s.
- Text and UI (drawer, sheet, notes, underlines): cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1), 240–600 ms.

TEXT
- Text is fully present from the first paint and never hidden behind a reveal.
- The H1 gets one gilt light-sweep (a background-clip text sheen, 1.2 s) whose angle follows the lantern. No blur and no per-letter splitting, so Cormorant's kerning survives.
- Log entries settle 8px from opacity 0.75 over 400 ms. Every in-between frame is measured at AA.
- Call lines keep the old timings: typing for 800 / 1,200 ms, 75 ms per word, a hold of 900 ms + 22 ms per character. They are revealed at scroll thresholds and completed in real time, so nothing is left half-typed on a fast scrub.

DURATIONS
- Lantern travel: critically damped, ω 5 rad/s (about 0.9 s).
- Window lights: a 640 ms filament flicker.
- Ring detent: under 450 ms.
- Ring docking into the cornice: a 900 ms FLIP.
- Lights down: 240 ms out, 120 ms hold, 420 ms in.
- Count-ups: 900 ms, ease-out cubic.
- Dawn: windows out in a seeded order over 4 s, with the sky following the clock.
- Start sheet: rises 16px while the backdrop dims to forest-950 at 60% with a 4px blur, 450 ms.
- Log drawer: 400 ms.

INTRO: THE PORTER'S LIGHT, 1.6 S
It never blocks content. The HTML is fully readable from the first paint, the H1 is the LCP, and a CSS still holds the lantern's place.
- When three.js is ready (loaded when the page is idle), a single warm point appears at the desk.
- The drawing's lines reveal outward from it (uReveal against distance from the lamp), and the windows light to match the visitor's real hour.
- The glass pours from empty to 56% in 1.8 s, and the ring's numerals tick from 18:00 to the visitor's 'now'.
- Any input finishes it at once. It is skipped on return visits. No percentage preloader.

IDLE LIFE (stopped by Pause)
- A window turns on or off every 6–12 s.
- Headlights sweep the street every 18–30 s.
- The lantern breathes and its bubbles rise.
- The ring's 'now' pin pulses once a minute.

TRANSITIONS
- Chapter to chapter: continuous with the scroll.
- Jumps of more than one chapter: 'lights down', with focus landing on the target chapter's heading (tabindex −1).
- Agent navigation while the visitor is reading: her second hand and a follow slip, never a jump.

REDUCED MOTION, AND PAUSE AS A USER CHOICE
The media query is listened to live. Pause motion is the Do Not Disturb hanger: aria-pressed, remembered per visitor (try/catch). It calls stage.setPaused, stops the gsap.ticker work, sets [data-motion=paused] to pause CSS animations, and stops call autoplay.

What changes:
- No camera rail: each chapter shows its settled pose through stage.still(). Still frames are redrawn on every state change, so voice states stay visible.
- No intro, no idle life, no lights-down fade: cuts are instant.
- No inertia, slosh, bubbles, lean or pendulums.
- Calls show complete, with a 'Next line' button.
- Count-ups and agent typing are instant.
- Lenis is off.

Scroll-linked position changes still happen, because the visitor drives them. The glass still turns in steps, and the ring still turns the night.

STACK
- Astro 7.3.8 (static), three 0.186.1 and lenis 1.3.27, as already installed.

- director.ts: owns time, sets camera, light and CSS variables.

- lantern.ts: the analytic glass, bubbles and flecks, the gimbal, and the backdrop pass.

- ring.ts: the SVG bezel, the slider ARIA, detents and the FLIP into the cornice.

src/scripts/voice/:
- session.ts: the app.js port.
- tools.ts: the seven tools plus the alias.
- presenter-hotels.ts: navigate, profile, roi, spotlight, recommend, fill and submit, implemented for the house.

src/scripts/apply/:

GPU AND PERFORMANCE BUDGET
Desktop target: 60 fps at 1440×900, DPR 1.5, on an Iris Xe or M1 class GPU.

GPU at most 8 ms per frame:
- house lines and windows: 1.2 ms;
- sky and city: 0.4;
- the lantern's backdrop pass (its rectangle only): 0.6;
- the glass quad at 420px: 1.2;
- bubbles and flecks: 0.4;
- threads and halos: 0.3;
- the key rack: 1.0, in its chapter only;
- the plate: 0.3, in the footer only.

Other limits:
- At most 30 draw calls, 80k triangles and 20 MB of textures.
- JavaScript at most 2.5 ms per frame.
- Phones: at least 50 fps on an iPhone 12 or Pixel 6.
- Initial JS at most 60 KB gzipped, without three. three.js and the house (about 170 KB gzipped) load when the page is idle. The SDK loads on intent.
- Fonts: Cormorant 500/600 (latin), Supreme 400/500, Ranade 500, plus about 8 KB of greeting subsets.
- LCP is the H1 text, under 2.0 s. CLS 0. INP under 200 ms.

RISKS AND FALLBACKS
1. Analytic glass quality. Budget 3–4 days and compare at three sizes against today's champagne preview. If it falls short, keep champagne.ts's MeshPhysical transmission at 0.5 scale (0.25 when small), with both looks precompiled; the translation then becomes a crossfade under a still.
2. The lantern's backdrop pass. camera.setViewOffset must stay correct on resize and DPR changes; it is covered by a Playwright alignment test at five sizes.
3. Contrast over a live canvas. Text sits only on the 88% scrim; the shader's luminance is clamped; the generator checks the worst case; Playwright samples rendered pixels at nine chapter poses across idle, lit, transition, paused and reduced-motion states.
4. DOM and 3D in sync. No getBoundingClientRect in the frame loop; projections are written as transforms only.
5. The ring driving the page. It uses immediate Lenis scrollTo, cancelled by any native input, and is tested at 60 and 120 Hz. Analytics show how many visitors turn it, and a config flag can make it decorative.
6. Generator scope. A parametric kit only; the default house ships first.
7. The moving talk button. The slip always offers the same action, and the orb button turns non-interactive when it is too small.
8. Unconfirmed content claims. 9. HubSpot is not ready. The adapter interface covers it, and the iframe is framed in our card rather than restyled.
10. iOS WebGL memory and context loss. Handled by the stage; textures are kept small.
11. Agent prompt drift. The page accepts the old tool arguments now. The ElevenLabs prompt update for the founders' offer, restaurants, the new section names and the allowlist hosts is an owner action in the same release.
12. Audio. Each 'Hear the night' button renders only when its file and alignment JSON exist.

- M2: the desk slip, start sheet, voice and text engine, and tools presenter, tested on localhost with the allowlist.
- M3: the NightClock, Director, ring slider and Night Dial, Night index, and lights down.
- M4: HouseStage with the default house, the analytic lantern and its physics.
- M5: the chapter theatre, annotations, phone threads and translation plate.
- M6: the generator, scenario chips and personalisation.
- M7: the handover, key rack, registration card and adapter.
- M8: sound, print, event layer, SEO, AVIF stills, audio if recorded, then QA.

QA viewports: 1440×900, 1280×720, 1920×1080, 768×1024 and 390×844, each in every state.

CUT LINE IF TIME IS SHORT
In this order: carrying by the bail, dispersion, stars and headlights, PMREM on the keys, then the translation plate (crossfade fallback). Never cut the voice, tools, ledger, application or accessibility work.

SCALE 1–10. Scored against the brief's bar (Awwwards SOTD+), the hard constraints, and the current codebase (stage.ts, input.ts, porcelain.ts, tokens).

A · "Twenty Minutes" (auteur, consultation + chart-recorder margin + sectionable model)
- Originality 8: the scroll as a recording medium and the openable porcelain model are genuinely new; the "visitor is the patient" ritual is a strong frame.
- Premium feel 8: radiology-workstation restraint, glaze lines, one key light; but the three-pane workstation (rail + viewer + lane + notes) is dense and risks reading as software, not a site.
- Clarity/usability 6: eleven chapters stamped in minutes, a 20-minute reading promise, a fixed pen, a minute ruler, a hinge, seven strata, a depth slider: a lot of apparatus between the buyer and the offer; the consultation metaphor needs explaining to be felt.
- Conversion 7: honest results table with payback and minutes is excellent; the 7-day Course with timings is the best onboarding device of the three; but the offer strip is only above the fold "at 1280×720 and up" and the register sits at minute 15.
- Feasibility 5: analytic ray-tracing of a sphere minus an octant plus a hinged octant piece, a lithophane relief texture, 30 depth-tested beads, a Float32 recorder lane and acquisition wipes is the heaviest shader and systems load of the three; the author flags the hinge as risk #1 with a cross-fade fallback.
- Performance 6: ~8 ray tests per pixel at 580×830 CSS × 1.5 DPR is at the top of the Iris Xe budget; the lane canvas plus HUD text at 10 Hz is fine.
- Accessibility 8: thorough live-region discipline, keyboard model for strata, range-input mirror, AA on drying words; the pen/lane and viewer are all aria-hidden with text twins.

B · "The Line" (inventor, one steel hairline = clinical line + phone line + drawing line; orb that cannot cross it)
- Originality 9: making the AI's safety scope a physical law of the page, drop-to-ask (pointing a voice agent at content with its body), and a two-sided transcript by responsibility have no precedent among the references or award-site tropes.
- Premium feel 8: no cards, no glass, three physical lights only, Newsreader for her voice; the lab spot-plate ledger is quietly luxurious. Slight risk of the ball-and-string toy reading as playful rather than clinical if the physics is bouncy.
- Clarity/usability 8: the split (hers / yours) is instantly legible and persists in every chapter; every gesture has a button twin; plain H2s throughout. Discoverability of pushing the orb is the one soft spot (mitigated by the 3.5 s hint).
- Conversion 9: the buyer's biggest fear is answered in the first ten seconds and again in 02 and 04; offer, ledger and guarantee are above the fold at 1440×900 and 390×844; payback drawn from the visitor's own numbers; honest minutes meter; calendar-on-page after qualification.
- Feasibility 7: 2D physics (fixed 120 Hz substeps, the same approach as the existing input.ts), a single scissored WebGL context, a 200-point SVG path for the line; the hard parts are line geometry across breakpoints and keeping the orb off text, both with stated fallbacks.
- Performance 8: orb fragment box ≤0.25 MP, plate ≤0.3 MP only while visible, no layout reads in the loop, loop idles at zero cost.
- Accessibility 8: WCAG 2.5.7 twins for every drag, a real button orb with described keys, polite status region, 1.4.11 measurements for the line and rings, forms with autocomplete and inline errors.

C · "The Line, in Porcelain: a monograph in nine plates" (editor, sundial-lit paperweight on printed plates)
- Originality 7: lighting a WebGL object from the visitor's real sky and reading the edition number off the object's underside are new; but numbered plates, crop marks, folios, a back-of-book index and a colophon are a well-worn editorial-site vocabulary, and its "Line" is a thinner version of B's.
- Premium feel 9: the most refined art direction of the three: "type never moves; light and object do", two inks, paper stocks, sidenote footnotes, modal-synthesis porcelain tinks.
- Clarity/usability 8: a book is predictable; Contents dialog; the lens toggle; the sentence-form profile is charming and clear.
- Conversion 8: reply card with embedded call, "what holds your place", payback footnoted, the mark as honest provenance; the edition label is above the fold.
- Feasibility 8: orthographic plan view with analytic shadow is cheap; no GSAP; CSS sticky pins; the author's own risk #1 (a plan-view sphere reading as a flat disc) is real.
- Performance 8: one scissored pass, 2 simplex + 2 Voronoi lookups per pixel, loop idles when nothing moves.
- Accessibility 8: shadow alpha capped at 0.16 with a generator check against the darkened page, no single-character shortcuts, status region discipline, container queries for 200% zoom.

VERDICT: B is the spine (highest on originality, clarity and conversion, and the most buildable of the ambitious ideas). C contributes its light (the visitor's sun and the night lamp), its provenance device (the underglaze edition mark), frost-as-privacy-glass and its contrast guard. A contributes the 7-day Course with timings, the lab-style results report, the physician call scripts, the consent statements and the "take the notes" summary attached to the application. A's hinged octant, lithophane relief and recorder lane are cut for feasibility.

final.big_idea:
THE DEVICE
A continuous 1px line in a new generated role --color-line (steel-600, 4.8:1 on porcelain #f5f7f9) starts under the top bar and ends as the baseline of the footer wordmark. It does three jobs.
1. The clinical line. Every chapter is split by it. AMARIYA's side is left (above it on phones); YOUR TEAM's side is right (below). It is the page's grid.
2. The phone line. Two plucked bursts travel down it when a call arrives; pulses run down it into the orb while she listens and up it away from the orb while she speaks; in the call room it becomes the recorded call's waveform.
3. The drawing line. It loops into a dial bezel around the orb in the features chapter, leaves its post to draw the visitor's own 30-day payback curve, ticks out the seven days of onboarding and the guarantee, and ends as the baseline under 'Amariya' with the orb as its full stop.
It behaves like a taut string. The orb dents it and plucks it. Push the orb hard against it and she does not cross; a hand-off slip slides over to the team's side: 'HAND-OFF · MEDICATION. Caller asks about ibuprofen before tomorrow's procedure. Callback requested. No advice given.' In a live call the same event fires when the agent calls show_handoff after declining a clinical question, so the visitor watches the real agent meet the line.

THE LIGHT (grafted from the monograph concept)
The orb is not lit by a studio. It is lit by the visitor's own time of day. The clinic's day runs 08:30–18:30 by default (the visitor can set their own hours in chapter 05). During the day a sun whose azimuth sweeps left to right across the page and whose elevation arcs with the hour lights the porcelain and casts a soft analytic shadow onto the page, across the type, so the screen reads as a sheet with an object on it. After hours there is no sun: the porcelain's inner steel light switches on and becomes the only light in the room, spilling a blue pool onto the paper. The old day/night copy swap becomes physics: 'After hours, she is the light.'

THE MARK (grafted)
The orb's underside carries an underglaze mark: 'AMARIYA · CLINICS · FIRST EDITION · No. 01 / 30', the number being the next open founding licence. Turn it over and read it. Scarcity becomes provenance, with no timers.

THE RECORD (grafted from the consultation concept)
As the conversation goes on, the page becomes the record: her actions stamp as mono margin notes on her side at the place they happened ('Calculated your estimate · 14:41'); hand-offs land as slips on your side; the profile rearranges the page; and at the end the visitor can take the notes, a printable letter of the conversation for the partner who was not on the call, attached to the application if they apply.

THE FIRST TEN SECONDS
One split headline across the line: 'The phone is hers.' left, 'The patient is yours.' right. The porcelain rests against the line inside four brackets, lit by the visitor's sun (or self-lit at night). Its frost thins where the cursor lingers. Grab it and it lifts, rolls (its engraved graticule really turns) and hangs from the line on a fine filament. Throw it right and the line dents, twangs and passes a slip across: 'Clinical question → your team. She doesn't cross.' The founding licence, the honest ledger and the guarantee are already visible in a mono ledger strip at the foot of the screen.

WHY THIS HAS NEVER BEEN DONE
On marketing sites an AI's limits are small print and orbs are ornaments that react to voice. Nobody has made an agent's scope a physical constraint you can test with your hand; let visitors point a voice agent at content by moving its body; lit a WebGL object from the visitor's real sky with a shadow that falls across the headline; split a transcript by responsibility so the page becomes a two-sided clinical record; or read a licence's number off the object's own base.

REFERENCES AND HOW IT GOES BEYOND THEM
- Neko Health's ECG line in brackets becomes the spine of the whole site and a physical boundary; brackets become the acquire language.
- Function Health's stat rows and comparison become the duty split in every chapter, a lab-style results report and a payback curve drawn from the visitor's own numbers.
- Clinic Beethovenstrasse's podcast card becomes a call room with recorded audio, a word-synced transcript and the orb as the stylus you scrub with.
- Superpower's objection and privacy block become a chapter you can test, not read.
- Clinique 7's turning object and qualifying question become a precision dial with six detents and a Medical / Aesthetic lens that rewrites the examples.
- Sky Clinics' 'Enable sound' bars: the line itself is the equaliser.
- Explore Primland's day/night toggle becomes the visitor's actual sky.
- Cartesia's inward-drawing listen, Igloo's frost and Octagos' milky porcelain become one material with four states and a privacy rule: the frost clears only during a live call and re-frosts when it ends.
- Biograph / Designjoy / Default: the price and what holds your place on one plate, the calendar on the page after silent qualification, the guarantee under the price.

One porcelain sheet, read top to bottom. Native scroll; Lenis 1.3.27 (lerp .1) on fine pointers only; native on touch and under reduced motion. Ten chapters, each a <section> with a stable id, a numbered landmark ring on the line (a link), and two sides in DOM order: AMARIYA first, then YOUR TEAM, each with a visible mono h3 label. Each chapter sets the line's x as a share of the viewport; between chapters the line S-bends over 240px of scroll (smootherstep). Only two chapters pin (01 story, 03 dial). Each chapter declares an orb anchor: a reserved empty grid cell on her side, tangent to the line, measured on resize; unless held, the orb rolls along the line to the next anchor as you scroll (rotation = path distance / radius).

PERSISTENT FRAME
Top bar (56px, opaque porcelain, hairline below). It is the conversation console and replaces the floating dock, so nothing covers the bottom of the content.

final.orb:
ROLE
The orb is Amariya's body and the page's only physical object: frosted porcelain with a soft steel-blue light inside, an engraved graticule, lithophane engravings, and an underglaze mark on its base. It does six jobs: talk button (click/tap/Enter); pointer for the conversation (drop it on anything to ask about it); dial (turn to choose a feature); playhead (scrub the call); proof of scope (it cannot cross the line); provenance (turn it over to read the next licence number). Home rule: it always rests on Amariya's side, tangent to the line, and it is lit by the visitor's own time of day.

NICHE TWIST: FOUR CLINICAL GESTURES
1 MOVE it: it rolls like a porcelain ball and hangs from the line by a fine filament, like a phone cord. 2 TURN it: a precision dial with detents, like a gauge bezel. 3 PRESS it against the line: it won't cross; it hands off instead. 4 TURN IT OVER: hold to grip, then roll it under your palm to read the mark on its base. Plus 'warm hands on cold porcelain': frost clears where the cursor lingers and slowly frosts back.

ONE GESTURE GRAMMAR (mouse, pen, touch)
- Tap / click (<6px travel, <250 ms): talk (the consent slip shows the first time) or end.
- Drag: CARRY. The orb lifts and moves with the pointer, rolling as it travels (ω = v/r about ẑ×v̂, integrated as a quaternion, so the graticule really rolls). Release over a landmark ring or a [data-ask] target places it there; released elsewhere it stays until its chapter leaves the viewport, then rolls home.
- Press and hold 280 ms with <8px movement: GRIP. The brackets snap closed, navigator.vibrate?.(6) on Android. Dragging now rolls the orb in place as a trackball (axis = normalize(cross(viewZ, delta)), angle = |delta| / R_px, the point under the finger stays under the finger). This is how you turn it over to read the mark. The existing OrbInput (yaw/pitch, DRAG_GAIN 1.6, pitch limit .55, inertia τ 1.1 s, spring k 16, 120 Hz substeps) is kept as the grip-mode integrator; carry mode adds a translation body.
- In the dial chapter the default drag is TURN (surface tracking Δθ = Δx/r, fling ≤12 rad/s, friction τ .45 s, detent spring k 90 c 16, vertical drag tilts ±25° with spring k 60 c 15.5); a vertical drag >64px pulls it out of the dial into carry.
- Near the cursor (≤1.8 r): it leans ≤8° toward it (τ 250 ms) and the four brackets close from 1.28 r to 1.12 r over 220 ms; the core light leans ≤.18R toward the cursor ('attentive'); frost thins 30%; cursor shows grab.

TOUCH-ACTION
- touch-action: none only on the circular handle (radius + 12px); the rest of the page scrolls normally. Before a grip, a vertical touch move that starts on the handle is handed back to scrolling (the existing root rule pan-y applies outside the handle). Magnet radius 72px on touch, 110px with a mouse. pointercancel releases cleanly. Hand-offs vibrate 8 ms when haptics are on.

KEYBOARD (the handle is a real <button>, 'Amariya, press to talk' / 'press to end', aria-describedby help)
- Enter / Space: talk or end. ↑/↓: previous/next point (the orb rolls, the page follows, status says 'Point 05 of 10: Your clinic'). ←/→: turn one detent (60° in the dial, 30° elsewhere); Shift multiplies to 90°. Shift+→ (Shift+↓ on phones): push into the line, perform a hand-off. End: turn over 180° to show the mark (900 ms); Home: set it down at rest. L: play this point's note. Esc: release or send home. ?: help. Single-character keys work only while the handle has focus (WCAG 2.1.4).
- Every gesture has a button twin: 'Push her across the line', 'Ask about this' on every [data-ask], a range input for the call, a tablist for the dial, 'Show the mark'.

PHYSICS (fixed 120 Hz substeps, semi-implicit Euler, dt clamp 1/30 s; constants in s⁻², s⁻¹)
- Lift on grab: z spring k 420, c 22 (ζ .54); scale 1 → 1.04; the contact shadow's offset 6 → 18px, blur 10 → 28px, opacity .22 → .12. Drop lands on the same spring with one small bounce.
- Drag: position = pointer − grab offset, τ 16 ms; velocity from an 80 ms window, cap 4000 px/s. Throw: v·e^(−dt/.32 s) until <40 px/s.
- Rolling: ω = v/r; after release angular friction τ .9 s; lean toward velocity ≤12° (τ 120 ms).
- Return / follow spring to the chapter anchor: k 140, c 19.4 (ζ .82), max 2600 px/s; scroll velocity adds ≤6° lean.
- Magnet to rings and drop targets: radius 110px (72 touch), k 320, c 25 (ζ .7), one small overshoot that reads as a click.
- Walls (viewport edges, the bar): k 900, restitution .35.
- The line: penalty spring k 520, c 18; dent is a gaussian 1.4 r wide, ≤28px deep; a hand-off fires at ≥24px penetration for 120 ms or ≥900 px/s impact; rebound restitution .35; 1.2 s cooldown; breaking contact plucks the line: a 7 Hz standing wave of amplitude min(14px, .012·v), τ .55 s.
- Filament: a 12-segment Verlet thread (1px, steel-400) from the nearest point on the line, slack sags under 1800 px/s² gravity, retracts on return.
- Grip inertia: least-squares ω over the last 80 ms, |ω| ≤ 9 rad/s, dω/dt = −ω/.85 s; a flick above 3 rad/s also rolls it ≤.5R along the flick, then the home spring (k 38, ζ .9) rolls it back.
- Radius per chapter: hero 132, story 110 (grows to a 56vh ring beat), call 40, dial 150, line 96, clinic 72, licence 64, apply/FAQ 56, footer a full stop; eases with k 60, ζ 1.
- Reduced motion: no inertia, no springs; drag is 1:1, release snaps or stays, the dial jumps, the line dents without vibrating, grip rolling is instant.

VOICE STATES (shape and motion, never colour alone; blend τ 90 ms; amp attack 40 ms, release 200 ms; tone τ 250 ms)
- Idle: core .38 r, frost 1.0, breathing on a 10 s cycle (±3%), self-turn .04 rad/s; one blip runs down the line every 8 s. Day: sun-lit with shadow. Night: self-lit with a pool on the paper.
- Connecting: frost 1.25; core .7×; a condensation ring contracts from rim to core over 1.2 s; dashes travel down the line from the bar at 600 px/s; status 'Connecting'.
- Listening: the core draws inward to .30 r and deepens toward orb-glow-deep (Cartesia); a clear diaphragm opens in the frost (r .45) so you see deeper into the porcelain; the visitor's mic level (getInputVolume, gain 2.2) contracts the core up to 8%; while level > .08 an inbound pulse runs down the line into the orb every 120 ms.
- Thinking: core −15% light; the orb turns itself at 25°/s ('turning it over'); a glint sweeps the graticule; three slow blips on the line.
- Speaking: core .38 r + .18 r·amp with the existing pressure rings (sin(24r − 5.5t)); the lithophane engravings light at .2 + .8·amp so her words literally light up the porcelain; the thin rim lets a faint glow through; outbound pulses run up the line toward the caption; the hairline in the H1 is also her trace (amplitude ≤6px, never touching the type).
- Muted: diaphragm frosts over (frost 1.4), status 'MIC MUTED'.
- Call ends: frost returns over 2.4 s, 'nothing of the call stays visible'.
- Tone from v3 audio tags: bright core +12%, engraving ×1.2; soft frost +20%, halo −30%; calm breathing 14 s, core toward steel-700; warm default (faint porcelain-cream centre, role orb-warm).

SCROLL AND CURSOR
When not held the orb rolls along the line between anchors (rotation = path/r, capped 1.2 rev/s, travel ≤.6 vw). Cursor warmth: frost clears to 30% in a .55 r spot facing the cursor (τ .6 s), re-frosts τ 4 s. While a carried orb hovers a [data-ask] element the brackets jump from the orb to that element (180 ms) and the nearest stretch of line catches its light. Status is always words in the bar and a polite live region; status never relies on hue.
final.three_d:
ONE CONTEXT
A single WebGL2 canvas fixed over the viewport, above content, pointer-events none, alpha, premultiplied, DPR capped 1.5 (1.25 coarse). It renders up to two views with setScissor/setViewport: the orb box (2.6 r plus its shadow ellipse and night pool) and the spot plate (480×360 CSS, only while visible). View rectangles are cached on resize and offset by the Lenis scroll value; no per-frame layout reads. The loop runs only while something moves (inertia, scroll delta, a call, a state blend) and stops when the tab is hidden, motion is paused or reduced. Context loss swaps in CSS stills. The line, filament, slips, brackets, hour ring, leader labels and notes are SVG/DOM so text stays sharp and accessible. A DOM <button> follows the orb by transform only and is the hit, focus and name target.

1 THE PORCELAIN (extends the existing one-pass porcelain.ts: orthographic quad, uRot mat3, SIMPLEX frost, core, rings, halo)
- Geometry stays an analytic ray-sphere hit in the orthographic view: n = (x, y, √(1−x²−y²)); object-space o = uRotᵀ·n from the physics quaternion (uploaded as mat3, replacing the euler in porcelain.ts update()).
- Sundial lighting (grafted): sun direction from local time t over 06:00–19:00: φ = π(t−6)/13 sweeps left→right; elevation θ = .18 + .62·sin(π(t−6)/13), clamped ≤1.1 rad so a shadow always exists. Wrapped diffuse (n·s + .35)/1.35; translucency at low sun pow(sat(−n·s), 2)·.25 tinted steel-100 (the far edge glows like porcelain held to a window); Blinn-Phong shininess 36 (frosted) → 140 (cleared); the existing milky Fresnel rim pow(1−z, 2.4)·.6. Dawn 05:30–07:00 and dusk 18:00–19:30 cross-fade into night; night uses the clinic hours once set in 05. Night: sun 0, ambient .35, the core emits a pool exp(−(d/2.2R)²)·.18 in role pool (steel-300).
- Paper layer in the same quad: the shadow of a sphere on the plane seen from above: an ellipse, semi-minor R, semi-major R/sinθ, centre offset R·cotθ along −ŝxy, penumbra blur .08R + .22·d; a crisp contact shadow exp(−(d/.35R)²)·.22; an AO halo R..1.15R at .12; total shadow alpha capped at .16 in role shadow-ink. The shadow spreads as the orb lifts (carry) and follows it along the line.
- Frost: 2-octave simplex on o×9 and o×23, amplitude .035·frost, where frost is a field = state frost × (1 − cursor warm spot) × (1 − listening diaphragm). Computed in object space so it turns with the sphere.
- Engraved graticule: latitude/longitude grooves every 30° (width .006, darkened 6%, a 1px bright lip on the lit side) so rotation is legible on a plain sphere. Glaze crazing (Voronoi F2−F1, one scale 5.5, width .018) adds +.25 specular along cracks on the high tier only.
- Lithophane: an R8 equirectangular texture 1024×512 drawn with Canvas2D after document.fonts.ready: six feature glyphs at 60° on the equator, the nine greetings on a +25° band, the clinic name on the front once known, '30' in the licence chapter, the wordmark at the end. Front light shows them as faint relief (normal perturbed by the texture gradient, strength .4); light from the core makes thin areas glow: T = core(n)·mix(.12, 1, th)·gain. Two textures cross-fade over 500 ms (uMix) when the chapter changes.
- Underglaze mark: a 512² CanvasTexture of Geist Mono ring text 'AMARIYA · CLINICS · FIRST EDITION' around 'No. 01 / 30', planar-projected on the underside (o.z < −.55, fade −.55..−.7), mixed in role underglaze (steel-700) at .85 with a .01 normal dent so it sits sunk in the glaze. Redrawn when the ledger changes.
- Core: the existing Gaussian core offset by the lean vector (≤.18), visible through frost at mix(.55, 1, clear), with the connecting contraction, speaking rings and tone uniforms; volumetric falloff along the chord so short chords near the rim let core light through while she speaks.
- One-time degrade (frames >20 ms, existing detector): one frost octave, no crazing, no relief emboss, DPR 1.

2 THE SPOT PLATE (licence ledger; one quad, ≤.3 MP, only while visible)
A porcelain laboratory spot plate with 30 wells (6×5) from a signed-distance field: concave wells with normals from the SDF gradient, ambient occlusion in each well, numerals 01–30 engraved below from a small R8 texture. uState[30]: open = clean empty well; held = engraved steel-700 ring, well lifted 4%; issued = steel-500 glaze with clear-coat specular (pow 64). Counts from niches.ts now, HubSpot later; nothing animates to suggest scarcity. A raking point light follows the cursor at a height of .15× the plate width (rests top-left on touch); the sun's azimuth sets its default. When the agent recommends the licence a slow light sweep crosses the plate (900 ms). Fallback: an SVG grid of 30 circles with the same states.

3 THE LINE (SVG, part of the same physical world)
Base geometry precomputed in page coordinates on resize and after fonts load from the chapter anchors: a polyline sampled every 4px including the dial loop, the payback detour, the course ticks and the footer baseline. Each frame where scroll or physics changed, the viewport slice (~200 points) is written into one fixed <path>, adding three offsets: the orb's dent, the string's vibration, and the voice trace (ECG-like pulses at 420 px/s). Near the orb the line catches its light (gradient steel-600 → steel-500 within ±1.2 r); a 1px soft shadow at 6% under the line makes it read as a string pulled taut just above the porcelain. In the call room the slice is the call's waveform from precomputed peaks (JSON, 20/s): played ink, unplayed steel-300.

4 THE HOUR RING AND DAY SHEET (DOM SVG)
The 24-tick hour ring (numerals every 3 h, Geist Mono 10px, aria-hidden) kept in register with the orb centre by ResizeObserver; the story's day sheet with a live 'now' tick.

TRANSITIONS
Line S-bends are scroll-driven (no timed animation). The orb radius springs per chapter. Lithophane engravings cross-fade 500 ms. The plate's light fades in as it enters. Hand-off slips are DOM: 320 ms translateX with a paper-like turn (rotateY 0 → −8° → 0). Sun changes are linear in clock time; the story's scrubbed sunset is scroll-driven; an agent time jump sweeps 1.6 s.

STILLS
At build time a Playwright script renders AVIF stills of each chapter pose at 09:00, 16:00 and 22:00 (OG image 1200×630 at 16:00 with the split H1; no-WebGL and Save-Data fallbacks; Index sheet thumbnails). The CSS still keeps the sundial: a tiny inline script sets --sun and --night so the fallback's blurred ellipse shadow rotates with the time, or a blue pool replaces it at night.

BANNED ON THIS PAGE
Particles, bloom, post-processing, fog, glass pills, gradient blobs, grain. The luxury is in the light and the material.
