- Arabic, Cyrillic, CJK and Devanagari greetings and the Arabic call use subset Noto Naskh Arabic / Noto Sans SC / Noto Sans Devanagari and system Cyrillic, loaded only near 01 and 02, with lang attributes.

COLOUR (Ink & Porcelain only; every new role through scripts/palettes.mjs with the AA gate)
Existing roles: bg-page ink-50 #f5f7f9; text-primary ink-950 #101f2e, text-secondary ink-700, text-tertiary ink-600; accent-solid steel-800 (Apply); focus-ring steel-600; orb-body/shade/glow-deep/glow/glow-hot/line.
New roles: --color-line steel-600 (4.8:1 as a graphic); --color-line-quiet steel-300 (decorative: unplayed waveform, future ticks); --color-landmark steel-700; --color-handoff-bg steel-100 / --color-handoff-text steel-800 (8:1); --color-note ink-700; --color-her-text steel-700 (her transcript words, AA on page and surface); --color-urgent-text red-700, only for 'call emergency services'; --color-shadow-ink ink-950 used at alpha ≤.16; --color-pool steel-300 (decorative); --color-underglaze steel-700; --color-orb-warm a low-chroma porcelain cream; --color-plate-glaze steel-500; --color-plate-well ink-200; --color-orb-engrave steel-200 rising to white, decorative.
Colour semantics: STEEL is only ever Amariya (her words, her typed values, the core light, the mark, the above-the-line list, the next cell); INK is the clinic's and the visitor's voice. Blue appears only as light: the core, its pool, the line where it catches the orb. No washes, no gradients behind text. The generator's PAIRS check is extended with 'text on page darkened by 16%' (the worst shadow) so the sundial can never break AA.

TEXTURE AND LIGHT
No grain: clinical cleanliness is the luxury. Depth from four physical lights only: the sun (or the core at night), the orb's contact shadow, the raking light over the plate, and the line's 6% shadow.

IMAGERY
No photography, no faces, no stock, no invented logos or ratings. The world is drawn: porcelain, hairlines, type. Proof is the working product, the ledger and real calls.

ICONOGRAPHY
Six custom glyphs, 1px stroke on a 24px grid, round caps: a receiver arc; a slot with a tick; two overlapping arcs; a ring with an arrow stopping at a bar; a circular arrow with a dot; two linked rings. Used engraved on the orb and inline. Control icons (mic, mute, send, end, close, sound) redrawn in the same stroke. Brackets (14px arms, 1px steel-700) are the language of selection.

OPTIONAL SOUND (opt-in, off by default, remembered per visitor, nothing before a gesture)
Join chime C5 → G5; landmark/detent tick 1.6 kHz 6 ms −30 dB; line pluck G3 (196 Hz) plus its octave, 600 ms, −24 dB; hand-off slip filtered noise around 1.2 kHz, 140 ms, −28 dB; porcelain settle tink (modal synthesis: partials 1 / 2.32 / 4.25 / 6.63, decays 1.2 / .6 / .3 / .15 s, gain .03) after a flick; call-room audio. All respect Sound off and Pause.

MICRO-INTERACTIONS
Brackets acquire the orb on hover/focus and jump to drop targets. The line dents and plucks. Landmark rings draw themselves (400 ms stroke) the first time reached. Agent-filled fields get brackets, a mono caret and '✓ NOTED'. Readout digits roll 600 ms, 30 ms stagger. Slips slide and settle. Stamps print with a 160 ms opacity step, no bounce. Buttons press 1px down, never scale; the Apply arrow is a short piece of line that extends 8px on hover. Fields are underlines (1px border-strong → 2px focus-ring), with visible mono glosses as real labels, 16px minimum.
final.motion_language:
PRINCIPLE: calm clinical precision. Only physical things move: the orb, the line, the slips, the light. Type never animates from invisible.

SCROLL PARADIGM
Native scroll; Lenis on fine pointers (lerp .1, autoRaf off, driven by the single scheduler); native on touch and under reduced motion. Two pins, both CSS sticky with progress computed from cached offsets and the Lenis value (no per-frame rect reads): the story (180svh) and the dial (210svh). Inside a pin something visibly changes at least every 6–10% of progress. Everything else flows. No dead scroll: every chapter ≤1.6 viewports; the orb and the line change at every chapter boundary.

EASING AND DURATIONS
--ease-settle cubic-bezier(.2,.7,.1,1) for UI; --ease-draw cubic-bezier(.65,0,.35,1) for strokes; physical objects use the springs in the orb spec. 140 ms micro (press, tick); 280 ms UI (panels, tabs; caption swap 120 out / 160 in); 400 ms ring draws; 500 ms lithophane cross-fades; 600 ms odometers and payback redraws; 900 ms intro line and plate sweep. Sun changes linear in clock time; the story's sunset scroll-driven; agent time jumps sweep 1.6 s; a jump >.35 of a pin snaps.

TEXT
No rising, no blur, no stagger cascades. Headings are 'printed': a hairline draws under the H2 left to right (600 ms, ease-draw) while the text goes from opacity .001 to 1 in 400 ms; content is always in the DOM and visible without JS. Margin notes type in mono at 18 ms per character. Numbers roll like a monitor readout. Agent typing 14–40 ms per character.

TRANSITIONS
The line S-bends between splits over 240px of scroll (smootherstep). The orb rolls along the line to the next anchor, its shadow and light continuous, and changes radius on a spring. The bar's state glyph slides with the line's x (transform only). Hand-off slips slide with a paper turn (320 ms). When the agent recommends, the plate's light sweeps (900 ms) and the orb turns over (900 ms, ease-turn cubic-bezier(.45,0,.2,1)).

INTRO (first visit only, ≤1.1 s, skipped by any input, never blocks LCP)
Text paints immediately; the line draws from the bar to the bottom of the viewport (900 ms); the orb falls 24px onto its anchor on the lift spring and plucks the line once; the brackets close; the core 'breathes on' (600 ms). No percentage preloader. Returning visitors see the line already drawn.

STATE MOTION
Breathing 10 s; the condensation ring while connecting; the inward draw and diaphragm while listening; the self-turn while thinking; rings and engraving glow while speaking; pulses along the line into the orb while she listens and out while she speaks; frost returning over 2.4 s when the call ends.

PAUSE MOTION (bar control, aria-pressed, remembered; also first item in the phone Index)
Stops every autonomous motion: breathing, line blips, story autoplay, call autoplay, line vibration, the plate's light drift, the filament sway, sound. Sets html[data-motion=paused] so CSS animation-play-state pauses. The orb freezes on a still frame that still shows its state and the current light; drag, turn and grip still work with fast settles (the existing OrbInput 'direct' mode).

REDUCED MOTION (live change listener)
No intro, no Lenis, no pins: the story's beats and the dial's details render as static stacked blocks with still renders at their hour; the dial becomes the tablist with a still orb showing the selected glyph. The line is static: dents show without vibration or pulses. The orb is a still frame per state; dragging has no inertia; grip rolling is instant. Odometers and agent typing are instant; slips appear without sliding; agent navigation jumps instantly; the sun is fixed at the current time; nothing autoplays.
final.mobile:
THE RULE ROTATES
On phones Amariya is above the line and your team is below it. The line runs down a gutter 12px from one edge; at each chapter's split it turns (24px radius), crosses the screen horizontally, and continues down the opposite gutter until the next split: a switchback. Each horizontal crossing is the boundary. Landmark rings mark chapter starts on the vertical runs.

THE ORB ON PHONES
In the hero it rests on top of the horizontal line like a ball on a shelf (r 64), lit by the visitor's sun with its shadow on the paper. After the hero it rolls into a cradle at the bottom right: r 30, a 64px target, 16px plus the safe area from the edges; this is the thumb's talk button. It slides out of the way while you scroll down and returns after 600 ms still or on scroll up. Drag it up onto Amariya's half of any chapter; push it down onto a horizontal stretch of line and she hands off (8 ms vibration). touch-action: none only on the handle; a vertical swipe that starts elsewhere scrolls. Hold 280 ms to grip for trackball rolling (and the mark). Dial: a horizontal swipe on the orb turns it through the detents, with the six mono tabs underneath. Call room: the transcript stacks; a horizontal waveform strip (32px) sits at the top of the chapter; scrub by dragging the orb or the range input.

LAYOUT AT 390×844
Bar 52px: wordmark, state glyph and caption, Apply, Index. Hero, all above the fold: the eyebrow and lens toggle; 'The phone is hers.' (44px); the line with the orb resting on it; 'The patient is yours.'; a 3-line lede; Talk and Chat by text side by side (52px tall); the ledger strip in two mono rows with Apply. On 667px screens the ledger strip falls just below the fold with a 'Founding licence ↓' hint.
Chapters: story pinned 140svh with the three beats compressed, the orb at 45vw in the top third with the hour ring partly off-canvas; dial unpinned (tabs plus orb); The Line as a full-width question list with slips landing below the horizontal line; Your clinic as the form, then the line, then the readout, then a full-width payback chart drawn by the line; Licence: price at 72px, the plate at full width (358×298), the ledger, the course ticks and guarantee on the line, the mark reveal when the plate centres; Apply: step 1 above the line, step 2 below, HubSpot embed 100% × 720px lazy; FAQ: the two groups stacked; footer: the wordmark sized to the width with the orb as its full stop.

PANELS
Notes is a full-height sheet from the top (the bar stays), composer pinned above the keyboard via visualViewport; Esc, close or the back gesture closes it. The start slip is a bottom sheet. The Index sheet holds the ten points, Sound, Pause motion and the lens.

PERFORMANCE AND ERGONOMICS
DPR 1.25; the plate at DPR 1; the lithophane 1024×512; one frost octave on the low tier (coarse pointer with hardwareConcurrency ≤4 or deviceMemory ≤4). No Lenis. Save-Data → stills only. 16px inputs, 44–52px targets, safe-area insets, svh units, scroll-padding for the bar and the cradle. Nothing important is drag-only.
final.feasibility:
STACK (all already in package.json): Astro 7.3.8 static; three 0.186.1; lenis 1.3.27; gsap 3.15 core + ScrollTrigger (used only for timed tweens: intro line, slips, plate sweep, mark turn; pins are CSS sticky with computed progress); @elevenlabs/client pinned to exactly 1.25.0 (change ^ to exact); Node 22.13.1.

ARCHITECTURE
- src/pages/clinics.astro takes precedence over [niche].astro for this slug (or [niche].astro hands 'clinics' to src/concepts/clinics/ClinicsPage.astro).
- Components in src/concepts/clinics/: TopBar, LineIndex, Chapter (split layout with data-split and data-anchor), Intake, Story (hour ring, day sheet), CallRoom, Dial, LineChapter (chips, slips, consent), Clinic (form + Account + payback), Licence (plate, course, mark caption), Apply, Questions, SignOff, NotesPanel, StartSlip, Letter (print view), FollowNote, Erratum.
- Typed data in src/data/content/clinics.ts: every string for both lenses, story variants, five call scripts with timestamps and audio URLs, the Line rule set, FAQ, ROI constants, course, consent statements, an owner-confirm Pending<T> marker that fails the production build if still present. src/data/agent/clinics.ts: greetings, agentContext, tool enums.

SCRIPTS
- Shared voice engine src/scripts/voice/{session, state, tools, roi, apply-adapter, context, events}.ts with a per-concept Presenter interface (navigate, profile, roi, spotlight, recommend, fill, submit, handoff?); src/concepts/clinics/presenter.ts.
- line.ts: geometry from DOM anchors (ResizeObserver on main, debounced 100 ms, recomputed after fonts.ready), the viewport-slice renderer, dent, vibration, voice trace, waveform mode.
- physics.ts: the translation body (lift, drag, throw, roll quaternion, home/follow spring, magnets, walls, line contact, cooldown), the Verlet filament, fixed 120 Hz substeps; reuses the existing OrbInput for grip-mode rotation and the dial's detent integrator.
- orb-handle.ts: pointer grammar (tap / carry / grip / dial), keyboard, magnet targets, [data-ask] hit testing against cached rects.
- sun.ts: time → light vectors and shadow params; clinic hours; --sun / --night CSS variables for the still.
- field-stage.ts extends OrbStage: OrbState gains 'connecting' | 'thinking'; setTone(); amp applied while listening (today stage.ts zeroes it unless speaking); setOrientation(quat) / getOrientation(); setView(rect) with scissor per view and a second view for the plate; an external-tick mode where the scheduler calls step() and draw(); keeps the IntersectionObserver, visibility pause, context-loss handling, DPR caps and the one-time degrade. boot.ts: [data-orb-talk] calls requestStart instead of the preview simulation; the old level hook renamed to data-level.
- porcelain-line.ts extends porcelain.ts (sundial lighting and paper layer, graticule, crazing, lithophane with uMix, underglaze mark, lean vector, tone/bands uniforms); lithophane-texture.ts and mark-texture.ts (Canvas2D); plate.ts (SDF shader).
- scheduler.ts: one rAF loop (gsap.ticker as the single driver). Order each frame: lenis.raf → physics substeps → line slice → stage draw. Reads first, then writes. The loop idles at zero cost when nothing moves.
- navigator.ts: Lenis/native scroll owner with goTo(section | sub-position, {fromAgent}), the polite-follow rule, hash updates, instant jumps under reduced motion.

BUDGETS
- LCP ≤2.0 s on 4G: the H1 text; Newsreader 300 Latin subset preloaded; fonts never block. CLS 0: every canvas and slot reserved.
- Initial JS ≤35 KB gzipped (line, bar, handle, 2D physics, clock). three + shaders ~130 KB gzipped tree-shaken, idle-loaded. GSAP core + ScrollTrigger ~45 KB idle-loaded. The ElevenLabs SDK (with livekit) only on intent. HubSpot iframe after qualification.
- GPU: orb ≤.25 MP fragments per frame (r 132 at DPR 1.5, box 2.6 r plus shadow); plate ≤.3 MP only while visible; one context. Per pixel inside the sphere on the high tier: 2 simplex + 1 Voronoi + 2 texture samples; target <2 ms on Iris Xe at 1440×900, 60 fps on M1, iPhone 12, Pixel 6, with the degrade as a safety net.
- Main thread ≤4 ms per frame; no layout reads in the loop; the line slice ~200 points; HUD text updates ≤10 Hz.

TESTS
Physics unit tests (line contact, hand-off thresholds, detent snapping, cooldown). ROI vectors (4 practitioners → 150 / $16,313 / 50 h; payback ≈6.5 days; 750 / 3,000 minutes). Sun tests (06:00, 12:00, 18:30, 23:00 → expected azimuth/elevation/night). Playwright stills at 1440×900, 1366×768 and 390×844 at 09:00, 16:00 and 22:00, in every state and under reduced motion; an axe pass; a contrast pass over the rendered stills including the shadowed headline.

BIGGEST RISKS AND FALLBACKS
1. Gesture discovery (carry vs grip vs dial). Mitigation: the 3.5 s hint, visible button twins everywhere, help on focus, one grammar across chapters; the dial's drag-to-turn is explained by the bezel itself.
2. Line geometry across breakpoints and changing content (form errors, FAQ opening). Mitigation: recompute on ResizeObserver(main) debounced; if a special segment won't fit, that chapter falls back to a straight line.
3. The orb landing on text. Mitigation: anchors in reserved cells; the orb only covers text where the visitor puts it; carry releases over text roll home when the chapter leaves.
4. The sundial shadow hurting contrast. Mitigation: alpha cap .16, the generator check against the darkened page, review stills at noon and dusk.
5. A plan-view sphere reading flat. Mitigation: minimum sun elevation leaves a shadow, the crisp contact line, far-edge translucency, the graticule turning under rotation; fallback a 12° fake oblique applied in the shader only.
6. Physics instability with stiff springs. Mitigation: fixed 120 Hz substeps, velocity caps, the hand-off cooldown, dt clamp.
7. Touch grip vs scrolling. Mitigation: pan-y everywhere except the handle; grip only after a held press; tested on iOS Safari and Android Chrome.
8. The agent contract. The seven old tools work unchanged; show_handoff, show_the_line, play_call, show_register, take_notes and the new ids are dashboard additions made together with the prompt update (clinics wording, founders' offer, extended safety rule); the agent allowlist gets dev, preview and production hosts.
9. Unconfirmed claims: privacy/recording terms, HIPAA/GDPR posture, emergency routing and numbers, guarantee terms, the overage rate, multi-location rules, reply times, physician ROI values, call audio. Mitigation: typed Pending slots that block production; nothing invented.
10. No WebGL2, lost context, Save-Data. Mitigation: the CSS still (with its time-rotated shadow) sits inside the same handle and is still draggable; the line still works; the plate falls back to SVG; 3D is never required for any task.
11. No JS. All chapters readable as static HTML (story stacked with a static time, dial as a list, first call static, FAQ native); the application posts to /api/apply once the server route exists; until then a noscript notice gives an email link.
final.accessibility:
STRUCTURE
One h1 with both halves in one element; an h2 per chapter; visible mono h3 labels 'Amariya' and 'Your team' on each side; DOM order left side then right. Landmarks: header (bar), nav (switcher), nav (points / line index), main, aside 'Conversation with Amariya' (Notes), footer. Skip link 'Skip to content' → #story. Decorative layers aria-hidden (the line, filament, plate, engravings, hour ring, shadow) each with a text equivalent: the ledger sentence, the payback sentence, the greetings list with lang attributes, the time in the bar and in the beat copy, the mark's text in a caption once revealed and in 06.

THE ORB
A real <button> named 'Amariya, press to talk' (ends 'press to end' during a call), aria-describedby help listing the keys. Focus ring: 2px focus-ring circle at 4px offset plus the brackets closing, measured ≥3:1 on page and surface. The keyboard covers every gesture; single-character keys act only while the handle has focus (WCAG 2.1.4). WCAG 2.5.7: every drag has a single-pointer alternative: 'Push her across the line', 'Ask about this' on every [data-ask], a range input for the call, a tablist for the dial, 'Show the mark'. Arrow keys never trap Tab.

LIVE REGIONS
A polite status region (role=status) announces only connecting and connected, muted and unmuted, mode switches, the end of a call with its reason and duration, 'Placed on point 05: Your clinic', 'Handed to your team: medication question', 'Placed below the line: this goes to your clinician', and model changes requested by keyboard. It never announces every listening/speaking flip. The thread is an ol with aria-live polite; the bar's caption is aria-hidden (duplicate of the thread); toasts go through the status region; the hand-off log is a list; the call timer is aria-hidden and announced once at the end.

MOTION
Pause motion in the bar and in the phone Index (aria-pressed) stops everything autonomous (WCAG 2.2.2); prefers-reduced-motion is listened to live; nothing flashes (ring pulses ≤2.5 Hz); the clock's colon never blinks; no audio autoplays; recordings have captions and full transcripts.

CONTRAST ON RENDERED PIXELS
Every text pair comes from the generator and meets AA: ink-950 15.6:1, ink-700 6.9:1, ink-600 4.9:1 on porcelain; her-text steel-700 AA on page and surface; slips 8:1. New checks: text roles against the page darkened by the maximum shadow (16%). As graphics (1.4.11) the line measures 4.8:1 and the landmark rings 6:1; the unplayed waveform and engravings are decorative. No text sits over the orb, its pool or the plate. Placeholders are examples beside persistent labels, never the only label, and meet 4.5:1. Text never animates opacity from invisible, so there is no failing in-between state. Colour is never the only signal: her words carry a speaker label as well as steel; above/below the line has position plus a heading; register cells carry text plus a pattern plus an sr-only sentence; orb state is shape, motion and words.

FORMS
Native inputs, styled; chips are radio/checkbox groups in fieldsets with legends; labels always visible; autocomplete tokens (name, email, tel, organization); inline errors with aria-invalid and aria-describedby and plain wording; on error focus moves to the first error with a role=alert summary; on success to the result heading; agent typing never steals focus; the HubSpot iframe has a title and a text link fallback; without JS a noscript notice gives an email link until the server route exists.

TARGETS AND DIALOGS
Every control ≥44px (52px on phones); the orb handle ≥64px. Dialogs are native showModal (focus trap, Esc, focus returns). Esc also closes panels and sheets and releases the orb. FAQ uses native details/summary with the h3 outside the summary text; the dial's tabs follow the tablist pattern ('Feature 2 of 6: Bookings'); recording tabs likewise.

LANGUAGE AND SCRIPT
lang on the greetings and the Arabic lines; dir=auto in the thread; dir=rtl on the Arabic call; fallback stacks for Arabic, CJK, Cyrillic and Devanagari.

ZOOM AND REFLOW
Container queries switch chapters to one column at 200% zoom and 320px width; no horizontal page scroll (only the chip row scrolls inside its own region); scroll-padding keeps the bar and the cradle off focused elements.

NO JS AND NO WEBGL
All chapters readable as static HTML with designed stills; the CSS still keeps the sundial shadow; every task works without 3D.

dental.scores:
CONCEPT 1 "First Available (the Day Sheet)". Originality 9: the product page is the buyer's own daily artefact, time is the scroll axis and you can drop the agent into a gap; nothing in the reference set or the award galleries does this. Premium 7: the print discipline is right, but hatched bands, dashed drop zones and a 6x5 seat grid risk reading as a scheduling app. Clarity 7: the hour ruler and now line are strong wayfinding; the elastic ruler, six time bands and a dense first screen add load. Conversion 8: the offer is one entry above the fold, booking is diegetic at 18:00, payback and minutes sit on the tally, the seats are honest. Feasibility 7: one context with scissor anchors is sound; drop-to-fill physics, chair-column redraws and keyboard slot semantics are many moving parts. Performance 8: one pearl, one instanced mesh, SVG traces, no backdrop filters, one pin. Accessibility 8: sr-only chapter sentences, slot announcements and full key paths; the lane announcements must be rate-limited so they do not chatter.

CONCEPT 2 "The Strand (inventor)". Originality 7: pearl as scroll thumb, polish into a mirror patch and the grit-to-pearl morph are new; the page-long scroll-drawn line and the dot-map side nav are award-site staples. Premium 8: silk thread, jeweller's tray, three physical ledger states, burnished lustre. Clarity 6: six 160svh pins before the offer chapter, a three-way gesture ambiguity on one object, J/K and Shift modes to learn. Conversion 7: offer row above the fold and a qualifying question, but about ten viewports of pinned day before the licence. Feasibility 6: a DOM-driven CatmullRom Line2 rebuilt on every reflow, a lustre render target with two passes, seven draw calls plus bursts, a gesture-lock state machine. Performance 6: a fixed full-viewport canvas that animates whenever the thread is on screen, which is always; sixty iridescent instances. Accessibility 7: real ol transcripts and shape-coded states, but a scroll-thumb button with eight key bindings is hard to name, and the knots unpin only under reduced motion.

CONCEPT 3 "The Strand (editor)". Originality 6: plates, folio, colophon and specimen captions are the luxury-catalogue trope; the bowl physics, the string that vibrates with the voice and the blind-embossed time are original. Premium 9: asymmetric plate compositions, nacre orient overtones, a jeweller's lamp, emboss; the most refined art direction of the three. Clarity 8: numbered plates, a running head, the margin time rule, [ and ] keys; snap is confined to unpinned plates on desktop. Conversion 8: the strand ticket above the fold on every viewport, the practice-type selector personalises, the 7-day rule under the guarantee, honest "Application received". Feasibility 8: mostly CSS and SVG; the 3D is one pearl, a short tube and 39 small instances rendered only when their plate intersects. Performance 8: scissor to the pearl box plus the live string; no backdrop filters; two pins. Accessibility 8: landmarks, emboss aria-hidden with text equivalents, a polite region, the clasp steps aside near forms.

VERDICT: Concept 1 is the spine (it is the only one of the three that could not exist for another niche, and the only one with a device the visitor can play). Concept 3 supplies the craft (print emboss, cradle and bowl physics, nacre orient pass, the voice as a vibrating string, the practice-type selector, the 7-day rule, the clasp that steps aside). Concept 2 supplies the physics and honesty ideas (polish that changes the material, grit-to-pearl births, shape-coded ledger states, "What she never does", the insurance and knocked-out-tooth calls, the qualifying question). Two of the three concepts shared one metaphor (a strand), which is itself a sign that the strand is the obvious dental-pearl idea; the day sheet is not.
dental.novelty_check:
1. Time-axis page with a "now" line (Concept 1). Derivative of calendar apps (Google Calendar's red line) and of chronological scroll stories. Pushed: the sheet is typeset as print (serif numerals, 1px rose-gold rules, no boxes, no shadows, blind-embossed recesses), it rules itself in like a pen as you arrive, hours exist only where entries exist, the now line is a hairline with a stamped time rather than a red bar, and the chair columns redraw to the visitor's own practice. Nothing in a calendar does the last two.
2. Page-long scroll-drawn thread (Concepts 2 and 3). Derivative of Apple product pages and dozens of Awwwards sites. Cut as a page device. Kept only as the phone column's hairline, which during a live call tautens into a 3D rose-gold string that vibrates with the voice in three modes (Concept 3's idea). That is one moment with a job (the voice made visible as physics), not a progress bar.
3. Pearl as scroll thumb (Concept 2). New, but it collides with drop-to-fill (the same drag would both scroll and carry). Cut the scroll-thumb; kept carrying with edge auto-scroll (drag toward the viewport edge while carrying and the sheet moves under the pearl), plus J/K and PageUp/PageDown to jump entry to entry. The hour ruler is the scrollbar.
4. Dot-map side navigation (Concept 2) and plate/folio/colophon chrome (Concept 3). Both are tropes. Cut. Navigation is the hour ruler with appointment-book index tabs for the niches.
5. Polish via a 512x256 lustre render target (Concept 2). Novel and expensive. Pushed down to a uniform splat (centre direction, radius, strength) plus a global lustre value, which gives a visible mirror patch at near-zero cost; the decay is 20 seconds so the patch is remembered.
6. Giant footer wordmark. An award-site trope that is also a kept previous feature. Pushed: it is blind-embossed into the paper (colour equals paper, white and pearl-300 shadows), sits at the sheet's close with the pearl resting on its baseline leaving its last rose-gold trace, and never exceeds the fit formula. No white outline stroke.
7. Letter-by-letter resolve and fade-up stacks (old site). Cut. The signature entrance is ink-in: a clip-path wipe at 900px per second with the baseline rule drawing 80ms ahead. No letter splitting, no blur filters.
8. Greetings flying from the orb (old site). Kept because it demonstrates the multilingual claim, but re-staged as ink rolling off the pearl onto the paper, each with lang and dir, never overlapping.
9. "Opaline" sliding sheen and the physical-material pearl (GetLayers, Blob Mixer). Derivative at the material level. Pushed: the nacre has an orient pass (pink and green overtones at grazing angles), polish raises coherence, speech ripples the thickness in rings, and the material is handled (rolled, set, lifted), not watched.
10. Catalogue wink "Cultured rose pearl, 18 mm" (Concept 3). Cute, but it says jewellery, not dentistry. Cut.
11. The three-tier pricing grid, glass pills, blobs, marquee ticker and frosted dock from the old site. Cut entirely. The offer is a fee line on a treatment plan; the seats are recesses in the paper; the dock is the sheet's foot rule.
12. Tetri's Smile "Front Desk" (the competitor). They sell a persona with channel chips and a chat window. This sells a filled day on the buyer's own sheet. No persona avatar, no chips.

final.one_line: Your practice's own day sheet, opened at the visitor's real time and ruled in rose-gold, on which a nacre pearl that is Amariya rolls from call to call, sets a pearl into every gap your chairside team cannot reach, and can be lifted and dropped into any open slot to hear the call that fills it.
final.big_idea:
THE DEVICE. Every dental practice runs on one object: the day sheet. Columns are chairs, rows are ten-minute units, and the phone is the thing nobody is standing next to. All five buyer pains are rows on that sheet: the 7:45 toothache before the doors open, the insurance question at 9:10 while every chair is full, the 12:20 lunchtime reschedule, the 14:00 cancellation an overdue recall could fill, the 18:30 call after close, the 23:10 knocked-out tooth. So the site is the sheet. Pearl paper (#fbf5f5) ruled with rose-gold hairlines; the hour margin on the left is the navigation; the chair columns show the team's day as hatched busy bands; the phone column is where Amariya lives. She is a rosé nacre pearl resting in a blind-embossed recess at 07:45, the first available slot. As you scroll she rolls down the phone column over still paper, and every call she takes sets a pearl into a slot, so by 16:00 the phone column reads as a string of set pearls: the day, filled. The thirty founding licences are thirty recesses on the same sheet (open seats, held pearls, issued pearls), the application is booking the 18:00 slot, the FAQ is the notes column after close, and the footer is the sheet closing at 19:00 with the phone column still open. 'First Available' is the dental phrase and the offer at once.

WHY IT HAS NEVER BEEN DONE. AI-receptionist sites, including Tetri's Smile 'Front Desk', present a persona: a face, channel chips, a chat window, then stacked sections. Luxury product sites present an object to admire. Nobody has built the product page as the artefact the buyer already stares at every morning, with time as the scroll axis, the practice's own numbers rewriting the page (type '5 chairs' and five columns rule themselves in), and the agent as a physical object you can pick up and put into a gap in your own day. The hero is not an orb beside a headline; it is the top of a printed sheet dated today, with its first entry written at the visitor's real time.

WHAT IT BUILDS ON AND GOES BEYOND. From the previous site: the story at the visitor's own time (kept, now choosing one of six time-of-day scenes with the day and night clauses swapping live), the greetings leaving the orb (now ink rolling off a pearl onto paper), the agent typing into fields and moving the page politely (now writing entries onto the sheet in rose ink), the live-call demo (now the entries themselves), the orb as the talk button (now the pearl in its cradle). From the research: LAVA's onboarding timeline becomes the whole page; Designjoy and Default's calendar-on-page becomes the HubSpot slot at 18:00; Biograph's price plus what holds your place becomes one fee line beside the seats; Neko's status-per-market becomes thirty seats in three honest states; Son Daven's per-section scenes become hour rows; Clinique 7's one turning object becomes one pearl that is the agent's body and the main control; Blob Mixer's physical material becomes nacre with orient overtones that polishes under your hand; Sky Clinics' sound pills become an opt-in Sound toggle in the ruler. From the sibling concepts: the cradle and bowl spring, the voice as a vibrating rose-gold string, the blind-embossed time numeral, the practice-type selector and the 7-day rule (editor); polish with material consequence, grit-to-pearl births, shape-coded seat states, 'What she never does', the insurance and knocked-out-tooth calls and the qualifying question (inventor). It goes beyond all of them because the device is interactive and personal: the sheet is yours, the pearl can be carried, and every decorative element has a job (the ruler navigates, the now line tells the time, the seats are the ledger, the string is the voice).

final.orb:
ROLE. The pearl is Amariya: the agent's body in every state, the main talk control (a real button named 'Amariya. Press to talk; drag to roll her, lift her into a gap, or use the arrow keys'), the page's progress marker (it rolls down the phone column as the day passes) and the agent's pointer (it rolls to whatever she talks about). It is never a floating ball: it rests in a blind-embossed recess, casts a contact shadow, and moves by rolling. Nacre is the material argument: layered, warm, polished by handling, the dental pearl without a tooth cliche.

TWO HANDLING MODES, ONE OBJECT (extends src/scripts/orb/input.ts and keeps its constants: drag gain 1.6 rad per radius, inertia tau 1.1s, pitch limit .55 rad with a critically damped spring k=16, arrow keys .12 rad plus a 2.4 rad/s impulse, Home resets, touch-action pan-y on the root so vertical touch scrolls). IN THE CRADLE (the dental twist, part one): pointer down grabs; the pearl's centre follows the pointer 1:1 in pixels, limited to .65R from the recess centre with a rubber band beyond (displacement divided by 1 + 6 x over); it rolls without slipping, delta-theta = |delta-p| / R about the axis up x velocity, so it visibly rolls under the fingertip and leaves a rose-gold trace on the paper (an SVG path, 1px, fading over 2s). Release: velocity clamped to 1400px/s, a bowl spring returns it to the recess (k = 9 per s squared, damping ratio .7, one soft overshoot) with rolling friction tau .9s, integrated in fixed 1/120s sub-steps; a throw older than 120ms gives no inertia. Click versus drag: a press under 300ms moving under 6px is a click (start or end the conversation). LIFTED (the twist, part two): dragging along the lane axis past .65R for more than 60px, or a 350ms long press on touch, lifts the pearl out of its recess: scale 1.04, the shadow widens and softens, touch-action none only while lifted. It then follows the pointer along the lane (x locked to the lane centre, plus or minus 24px), open recesses in reach fill rose-100 in 120ms, and dragging within 80px of the viewport's top or bottom edge auto-scrolls the sheet at up to 600px/s so the pearl can be carried to any gap. Release within 40px of an open recess SETS it: a critically damped spring to the slot centre (k=28, c=2 sqrt k, about 350ms), a 6px dip into the paper, one ceramic tick (opt-in sound), the gap inks in its call and a contextual update tells the agent ('the visitor dropped Amariya into the 14:05 gap'). Release elsewhere: it rolls back to the nearest slot with friction. POLISH (the twist, part three): a slow circular rub in the cradle (radius at most .3R, speed at most 2R/s, held 400ms or more) ramps a lustre value 0 to 1 over 600ms: sheen .5 to 1, clearcoatRoughness .03 to .015, the thin-film thickness range narrows from [120, 820] to [260, 640]nm (more coherent colour), and a uniform splat (centre direction from the pointer through the inverse group quaternion, radius .35, strength ramping with lustre) drops roughness to .025 in the rubbed patch so it shows a sharp mirror of the room; lustre decays exp(-dt/8s) after the hand leaves, so a shine is remembered for about 20s. Cursor: within 1.5R the environment rotation nudges up to .25 rad toward the cursor (tau 250ms) so the highlight slides toward the hand, the dimple is .025 x hover, the bowl tilts .02R toward the cursor and the cradle's inset shadow deepens over 200ms; the camera yaws up to 3 degrees with the cursor (tau 400ms) for parallax against the ruled paper. TOUCH: a horizontal thumb drag rolls in the bowl and throws; vertical pans scroll the page (pan-y); a long press lifts for carrying; a tap talks; a slow circular rub polishes. KEYBOARD (focused): Left/Right roll in the bowl (.12 rad plus impulse), Up/Down pitch within the limit, Shift plus Up/Down carry to the previous or next slot (the polite live region says 'Slot 14:05, open, press Enter to hear the call'), J/K or PageUp/PageDown jump entry to entry (lenis.scrollTo 900ms, instant under reduced motion), Enter or Space set the pearl when carrying or start/end the conversation otherwise, hold P polishes the facing patch, Home returns to the now line, Escape drops. Focus ring 2px rose-600 at 10px offset plus the cradle darkening; a slot in reach gets a dashed rose-600 ring.

REACTIONS. States extend OrbStage to idle, connecting, thinking, listening, speaking, blended over 90ms, plus a tone input eased over 250ms. Idle: rests in the cradle, breathes plus or minus .4% at .15Hz, sheen sliding at .012 and .007 units per second, environment turning .06 rad/s. Connecting: lifts 6px, the contact shadow tightens to 70%, a rose-gold setting ring draws around the recess over 700ms, the environment spins six times faster so highlights streak. Listening: sheen toward rose-300, the dimple toward the cursor .07, the contact shadow becomes a halo whose radius follows the mic level (r = 1.1 + .25 amp, from getInputVolume), and the lane's hairline between the pearl and the sheet's foot tautens into a 3D string showing one standing wave with amplitude = input level x 3px. Thinking: a slow precession (yaw drift .4 rad/s) with the thickness offset scrolling four times faster so the nacre shimmers, plus a 3mm rock at 1.2Hz; the dock shows thinking dots. Speaking: scale 1 + .05 amp (attack 40ms, release 200ms), sheen .5 + .5 amp, nacre rings ripple from the crown at syllable rate (uRing), and the string vibrates with the output level in three modes (A1 = amp x 6px, A2 = amp x 2.5px, A3 = amp x 1px, decay tau 180ms, mode-1 at 3Hz visual). Tone from the audio tags: bright widens the thin-film range to [100, 900] and raises the highlight 1.3x; soft roughens the clearcoat to .12 and lowers sheen to .3; calm slows the environment to .03 rad/s and cools the sheen toward pearl-200; warm is the base. Scroll: the pearl is pinned at the reading line while the sheet moves, rotation coupled to displacement (rotation.x += delta-y / R) so it rolls over still paper; between entries it travels with tau 200ms and settles into the next recess with the bowl spring. State is readable without colour: lift, dimple, swell, rock, ring, halo, string, and the dock's words. Reduced motion or Pause: one still frame that still shows the state; the hand still turns it with no inertia, no rolling, no trace, no string.
final.three_d:
ONE WEBGL2 CONTEXT for the page: a fixed full-viewport transparent canvas behind the DOM, rendered only while something on screen animates (the stage's IntersectionObserver, visibilitychange and Pause gating), DPR capped at 1.5 (1.25 on coarse pointers), Neutral tone mapping, no post-processing. Scissor and viewport rectangles per anchor (the pearl box, the live string segment, the seats block, set pearls in view), so the fill cost stays that of one 320 to 360px sphere plus small instances; anchors are cached DOM rectangles updated by ResizeObserver and derived from the Lenis scroll value, never read per frame. One scheduler: GSAP's ticker calls lenis.raf then stage.step (scroll, physics, DOM writes, GL).

1. THE PEARL (hero 360px, lane 180px, footer 240px, dock 44px: one mesh re-projected per anchor, rendered 1.15x larger than its box with MSAA to kill the aliased rim). SphereGeometry 128x96. MeshPhysicalMaterial body rose-100, roughness .12, clearcoat 1, clearcoatRoughness .03, sheen .5 rose-gold, iridescence 1 with the tileable thickness map, IOR 1.3. onBeforeCompile extensions: a nacre orient pass (at grazing angles, fresnel squared, mix two overtone tints --color-orb-orient-rose and --color-orb-orient-green at 14% each, so it shows pink and green overtones like real nacre instead of a white ball); uRing for speech ripples (thickness offset += .06 x ring x sin(12 acos(dot(n, up)) - phase), phase advancing with amp); uLustre and uPolishPatch (centre, radius, strength) narrowing the thickness range, lifting clearcoat and dropping roughness in the patch; uTone (IOR 1.3 to 1.36 and highlight gain); the existing uDimple toward the pointer; a fresnel rose-700 edge at .16 with pow 4 (down from .32) plus a 1px DOM halo at pearl-200 under the canvas. Environment: RoomEnvironment through PMREM once at idle (under 30ms) plus one warm area light from the top left at 10% rose-gold so the specular reads as a jeweller's lamp; the environment rotates for the light sweep and the cursor nudge.
2. THE CONTACT SHADOW AND HALO: one plane with a small shader, pearl-950 at .2 for the shadow (scaled by lift), a rose-300 ring whose radius and opacity follow the mic level while listening, and a faint paper caustic (thin-film colour bands, opacity .12) that drifts with the environment rotation so the paper under the pearl picks up nacre light.
3. SET PEARLS AND SEATS: one InstancedMesh (max 64, sphere 32x24, the pearl material without clearcoat, iridescence .8) with per-instance attributes birth (0 to 1), thicknessOffset and scale. Vertex shader: a grit-to-pearl morph, position = mix(sphere + fbm3(position x 2.3) x .35, sphere, smoothstep(0, 1, birth)); fragment: iridescence and sheen scale with birth, a sheen flash x2 for 400ms at birth. A second InstancedMesh (max 32, matte variant: clearcoat 0, roughness .5, no iridescence) for held seats. Open seats are CSS recesses with no mesh. Each new set pearl is born over 1.2s ease-out quint. Two draw calls.
4. THE LIVE STRING: a TubeGeometry of 48 segments, radius .6px equivalent, MeshPhysical metalness 1, roughness .35, rose-gold, from the pearl to the dock, visible only during a call, displaced in a vertex shader by the three-mode standing wave y(x,t) = sum of A_n sin(n pi x / L) sin(2 pi n 3t + phi_n) with per-mode decay. Outside a call the same path is the lane's 1px SVG hairline, so there is no per-frame curve rebuild.
5. THE ROLL TRACE, the drawn hairlines and the seat rings are SVG paths in the DOM (stroke-dashoffset), crisp and cheap. The blind-embossed numeral, the cradle and the wordmark are CSS, not GPU.
6. GREETINGS are DOM text moved with transform and opacity only (no filter blur), appearing rose-gold and settling to ink over 200ms.
TRANSITIONS: scissor rectangles change per frame; the pearl's scale and camera distance interpolate (tau 200ms) when it moves between anchors; while it travels the chair bands stay still, which reads as rolling over paper. Chapter births: grit to pearl 1.2s with the sheen flash. Agent spotlight: the target entry's pearl rises 8px with a sheen flash and the slip opens; only one lit at a time. FALLBACKS: without WebGL2 the existing CSS pearl still sits in the cradle and SVG pearl marks draw the seats and the lane; context loss pauses and drops is-live; the one-time degrade (frames over 20ms after 1.5s) sets DPR 1, iridescence .6, sphere 64x48, instances to MeshStandardMaterial and polish to lustre only.

final.art_direction:
GRID. Desktop: a 96px hour ruler plus a 12-column sheet, 24px gutters, 1280px max; chair area columns 1 to 7, phone lane 8 to 12; baseline 8px; rows separated by 1px rules, never boxes; chapters composed asymmetrically on the sheet (the lane always on the right, text widths 5 to 7 columns), never centred stacks. The sheet reads as print: no shadows except the pearl's contact shadow, no glass, no gradients except the cradle's radial, no cards, no pills.
TYPOGRAPHY (no italics anywhere; a global rule sets em, i, cite, dfn, var and address to normal; font-synthesis none; em rendered upright in rose-700). Instrument Serif 400 for display only: h1 64/56/42 at 1.0 and -.012em, chapter times 64 (current) and 22 (others), tally figures 34 in fixed-width digit cells (Instrument Serif has no tabular figures), date 32, entry titles 28, the embossed time numeral clamp(8rem, 22vw, 18rem). Supreme for everything else: lede 19/1.5, body 17/1.5, slip values 16, labels 13 small caps tracking .08em, eyebrow 12 tracking .16em, marginalia 12 caps; tabular-nums on every time, timer, count and price. Ranade 500 only for the brand and the embossed wordmark. Arabic, Urdu and Japanese greetings carry lang attributes and a serif system fallback stack.
COLOUR within Rosé and Pearl, all through scripts/palettes.mjs and measured on the page: paper pearl-50 #fbf5f5; ink pearl-950 #2c1818 (about 14:1); secondary pearl-700 (7.2:1); marginalia pearl-600 (measured at or above 4.5:1); accent text, links and the one filled button rose-700 #7d424e (7:1, white label 7:1), rose-800 hover; focus ring rose-600 #a05161; rose-100 for subtle fills (the ink wash, selected chips). Rose-gold #d09e83 is hairlines, seat rings, caps and the string only, never text. New roles added to the generator: --color-rule (rose-gold, decorative), --color-now (rose-600, 5:1 as a UI line), --color-band and --color-band-edge (pearl-100 and pearl-200 for chair bands), --color-band-hatch (pearl-300 diagonal 1px lines at 6px pitch), --color-ink-wash (rose-100 behind agent-typed text, rose-700 on it 6.2:1), --color-seat (pearl-500 ring for open recesses, 3.3:1), --color-emboss-light (white) and --color-emboss-shade (pearl-300), --color-paper-shade (pearl-100 for the cradle), --color-paper-evening (pearl-100 for the after-hours chapters, all pairs re-measured), --color-orb-orient-rose and --color-orb-orient-green (decor), --color-string (rose-gold, decor).
TEXTURE: a laid-paper SVG noise at 3% opacity, fixed, multiply (dropped under 734px); blind-emboss effects for the cradle, the time numeral, the seats and the wordmark; a 1px perforation row under the header; nothing else.
IMAGERY: none. No stock, no renders, no teeth. The pearl, the ruled sheet and the type are the imagery.
ICONOGRAPHY: typographic markers first (numerals, middle dots, rules); where a glyph is needed (tick, handset, moon, speaker, keyboard, microphone, mute, end, send, close) hand-drawn 1.25px hairline glyphs on a 20px grid drawn for this site as inline SVG with stroke-dashoffset reveals, rose-700 on hover; decorative glyphs aria-hidden; no icon library in content.
OPT-IN SOUND (off by default, remembered per viewer, silenced by Pause and reduced motion): a ceramic tick (40ms, -18dB) when a pearl sets, a 300ms filtered-noise hush at gain .03 when a polish completes, the two-note join chime, a paper tap on an outcome stamp, real call audio when supplied; nothing autoplays.
MICRO-INTERACTIONS: hovering an entry darkens its text one step and draws a 14px rose-gold left tick (180ms); links underline by drawing a 1px rule from the left over 220ms; the filled button lifts nothing and only deepens to rose-800, pressing to scale .98; ghost controls are 1px pearl-500 outlines; form fields are baseline rules that turn rose-700 and 2px on focus and glow rose-gold while she types; outcomes stamp (scale 1.15 to 1, rotate -4 to -2 degrees, 160ms); slots in reach pulse a dashed ring once; the tally figures count up; the now label slides on the minute (350ms); index tabs pull forward 2px on hover; the cradle deepens on hover; the seat nearest the cursor tightens its ring.
final.motion_language:
SCROLL PARADIGM: scrub through a day on one sheet. Lenis (lerp .09, desktop fine pointers only, native-scroll mode so position fixed stays fixed) feeds GSAP 3.15 ScrollTrigger; the only pinned scene is 07:45 (220svh, scrub .6); everything else triggers on the reading line (38svh) and the pearl travels between recesses with tau 200ms. Native scrolling on touch and under reduced motion; no snap anywhere. Agent navigation and ruler links use lenis.scrollTo with duration clamp(|distance| x .45, 500, 1100)ms and ease-in-out cubic, cancelled by any visitor input, instant under reduced motion, targeting a chapter's state (the pin's progress) not only its top.
EASING AND DURATIONS: one UI curve cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1); micro 180ms, controls 350ms, entries 700ms, chapter fills 240ms per band at 60ms stagger; physics for the pearl (bowl k=9 zeta .7, set spring k=28, pitch spring k=16, friction tau .9s, inertia 1.1s), never tweens. The signature is INK-IN: every sheet entry appears as a left-to-right clip-path wipe at 900px per second, like a pen line, with the rose-gold baseline drawing 80ms ahead of the text; no letter splitting, no blur filters, no fade-up stacks; text is at AA in every in-between state because the wipe reveals finished ink. Figures count up over 900ms ease-out cubic. Things Amariya writes type per character at 14 to 40ms.
INTRO (1.5s, skippable by scroll, no preloader; the still pearl and all type are in the first paint): paper opacity 0 to 1 over 300ms; the header rule draws from the left over 600ms; the date stamps in (scale .96 to 1, 300ms); ruler ticks draw top to bottom at 12ms stagger; when the scene has loaded the canvas fades in over 1.4s and the pearl rolls in from the left along the 07:45 row and settles into its cradle with the bowl spring (one overshoot); the first entry inks in at 1.1s.
TRANSITIONS: no section gaps; chair bands are continuous so the pearl's travel is the only transition; the after-hours chapter warms the paper over 600ms as it crosses the reading line; set pearls are born from grit over 1.2s with a sheen flash; the agent's spotlight lifts a pearl 8px; the footer's wordmark rises 24px while the pearl rolls to its baseline.
REDUCED MOTION (listened for live): no Lenis, no pin (the three beats stack as written entries with the current time), no ink wipes (entries visible), no rolling, trace or string, the pearl a still frame that still shows state and turns under the hand without inertia, greetings as a static multilingual line, calls static with their first exchange, the now line static with its label updating on the minute, counts and typing instant, agent navigation jumps, the seats static. PAUSE MOTION (the ruler's control, global [data-motion=paused]): animation-play-state paused on every CSS animation, GSAP's global timeline paused, stage.setPaused(true), the level loop, call playback, the colon blink, the sheen slide and the greetings stopped; status text and the clock keep updating; a paused pearl still rolls under the hand without inertia.

final.feasibility:
BUILD. Astro 7.3.8 static pages; src/pages/dental.astro composes the chapters under a DaySheet layout that extends Base.astro with the ruler, header, edge tab and dock. Components: DaySheet (grid), HourRuler, SheetHeader with IndexTabs, StoryRow (07:45), PracticeChips, IntakeSlip and Tally, WorkingDay with PhoneEntry and DropZone, NeverDoes, LicenceLine and Seats, ApplySlip with the HubSpot embed, NotesColumn (FAQ), Close, Dock, CallSlip (transcript), StartSlip (consent), FollowNote, Toast. Content in a typed src/data/content/dental.ts (every string, the six time-band scenes, the six entries with scripted calls, the never-does lines, the FAQ tabs, the greetings and the SEO block required by its interface, so a missing field fails the type-check; owner-confirmed slots render nothing until filled). Colours only via --color-* tokens with the new roles added to scripts/palettes.mjs and regenerated. Scripts: sheet/scroll.ts (Lenis on fine pointers, GSAP ScrollTrigger for the single pin, the anchor cache on ResizeObserver, the navigator with the five section names and the polite rule), orb/stage.ts extended (connecting and thinking states, tone, a listening amp path, scissor anchors, a scene registry holding the pearl, shadow plane, two instanced meshes and the string), orb/input.ts extended with the cradle bowl, lift and carry, slot snapping, the click threshold, polish detection and the extra keys (same fixed sub-step integrator), orb/pearl.ts extended with the orient pass, ring, lustre and patch, tone uniforms and the halo plane, strand/string.ts (the tube and its wave), voice/session.ts (the ported engine, typed, guarded lookups, @elevenlabs/client 1.25.0 lazy), voice/tools.ts (the seven client tools plus the alias behind a sheet presenter: navigate, profile, roi, spotlight, recommend, fill, submit), apply/adapter.ts (local plus console now, a POST to an Astro server route for HubSpot later, keys never in the client), events.ts, clock.ts (ported verbatim with the day/night re-check in tick).
PERFORMANCE BUDGET: initial JS under 60kB gzipped before idle (no three, no SDK); three core plus addons (about 170kB gzipped) and the pearl scene load at requestIdleCallback with a 1500ms timeout behind the CSS still; the SDK on warm-up only; LCP is the h1 text; the pearl's box is reserved so CLS is 0; one WebGL2 context, DPR 1.5 (1.25 coarse); draw calls per frame: pearl, shadow plane, set-pearl instances, held instances, string (calls only), at most five; under 120k triangles; scissor rectangles under 25% of the screen; target 4ms GPU on Intel Iris Xe and 8ms on a 2019 mid-range Android at DPR 1.25; memory under 50MB with the PMREM; offscreen and hidden-tab pausing, the one-time degrade, context-loss handling, no per-frame layout reads (anchors cached on resize and derived from the Lenis value); CSS animations only on transform, opacity and clip-path; no backdrop-filter anywhere. Previews at 1440x900, 1366x768 and 390x844 before any deploy, one chapter at a time on the 6GB machine with short headless runs; nothing committed, pushed or deployed by the build agent.
RISKS AND FALLBACKS. (1) The sheet reads as a calendar app: the print art direction (serif numerals, hairlines, emboss, no boxes, no shadows) is the guard, checked in previews. (2) The elastic ruler confuses: only hours with entries get labels, ticks are evenly spaced between them, the now label always says the real time. (3) ScrollTrigger plus Lenis on iOS: native scroll on touch, the pin uses position sticky with scroll-derived progress, no scroller proxy on touch. (4) Lift versus scroll on touch: the lift needs a 350ms long press and shows a carrying state; a plain swipe always scrolls. (5) Iridescence on Mali and Adreno: the degrade path and the orient pass carry the look at iridescence .6; without WebGL2 the CSS still, the SVG lane and the CSS seats keep the concept intact. (6) The HubSpot iframe cannot be styled or pinned: it sits unpinned in its own block with a min-height and a loading note. (7) Agent contract: tool names, enums and section names are kept and the plan keys mapped on the page; the dental prompt, the founders' offer, the never-does rules and the allowlisted dev, preview and production hosts must be updated in the ElevenLabs dashboard in the same release (owner action). (8) Unconfirmed claims (the minute overage rate, multi-location terms, privacy and recording wording, the insurance scope, reply time, real call audio, HubSpot counts, the $3,000 price) are copy slots that render nothing until the owner fills them.
final.accessibility: SEMANTICS: the sheet is a sequence of sections with ids, not a table; the ruler is nav[aria-label='The day'] with real links and aria-current; landmarks (header, nav, main, aside for the dock, footer); one h1, an h2 per chapter, h3 per entry and question; the skip link goes to #profile; times are text; the chair bands are aria-hidden decoration with one sr-only sentence per chapter ('An example day: two chairs busy from 8 to 5'); every call slip is a real ol with dir=auto and lang on Spanish and Arabic lines; greetings carry lang; the embossed numeral, the wordmark and all 3D are aria-hidden with the sentence carrying the time in text; the seats have a text equivalent ('30 founding licences, 0 issued, 0 held, 30 open'). THE PEARL is a real button with a name that includes the brand and the state, aria-pressed while a call is live, a 2px rose-600 focus ring at 10px offset plus the cradle darkening so focus is visible on pale paper; a polite live region announces its position only during keyboard carrying ('Slot 14:05, open, press Enter to hear the call') and conversation milestones (connecting, connected, muted, ended, errors), never every listening and speaking flip; the transcript ol is aria-live polite; toasts are role=status; the activity log records what she did to the sheet. CONTRAST on rendered pixels: ink about 14:1, secondary 7.2:1, marginalia at or above 4.5:1, accent 7:1, evening paper 13.7:1 and 6.3:1, agent-typed text 6.2:1 on its wash, seat rings 3.3:1, the now line 5:1; rose-gold is never text; no text ever sits on the pearl; entrances are clip wipes of finished ink, so no state leaves type below AA; placeholders are replaced by persistent examples. TARGETS at least 44px everywhere (dock controls, tabs, chips, seats, hour links). KEYBOARD covers everything the pointer does: roll, carry, set, polish, open an entry, jump entries, tabs, details/summary, the dialog with its focus trap and Esc, Esc for the transcript. STATE is never colour alone: pearl states carry shape and motion (lift, dimple, swell, rock, ring, halo, string) and the dock carries words; seat states carry shape and material. MOTION: a visible Pause motion control pauses everything on the page (WCAG 2.2.2), prefers-reduced-motion is honoured and listened to, still frames still show state, sound is opt-in and never autoplays. FORMS: labels wrap inputs, 16px type, inline human errors tied by aria-describedby ('Please add a valid email address'), the success state takes focus with honest copy, the application posts to a real route so it works without JavaScript once the server route exists. CONTENT is never covered by the dock (reserved padding, the knob near fields and the close). HONESTY: no fabricated records, logos, ratings or recordings; the only proof is the seats, the guarantee and the calls; a note marks the example day as illustrative.
